findings.title: /spend footnotes permanently name healthy butlers as 'unavailable' — classify-before-flagging violation (switchboard proven)
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/spend/by-schedule → meta.unavailable_butlers=['messenger','qa','switchboard'] while GET /api/butlers reports all three status 'ok'. Root cause proven for switchboard: roster/switchboard/butler.toml:15 (and live GET /api/butlers/switchboard/runtime-config) deliberately omits the 'scheduling' and 'sessions' core_groups (0 LLM calls audit 2026-04-07), so the schedule_costs / sessions tools are never registered on its MCP; spend.py:1001 catches blanket `except (ButlerUnreachableError, TimeoutError, Exception)` and marks the tracker, so a legitimately-absent tool is flagged as a degraded source. CLAUDE.md degraded-envelope convention explicitly forbids this direction: 'A source that is legitimately absent … is not a degraded source — only flag a genuine failure.'
findings.detail: Consequence: every /spend surface (by-schedule, daily, top-sessions, summary) will footnote switchboard as 'cost source unavailable' forever, on every page load, while switchboard is healthy. Permanent false alarm trains the owner to ignore the footnote — the exact erosion of earned calm the honesty program was built to prevent, now shipped at fleet scale by that same program's consumer wiring (bu-jad4j.3/bu-h3ej9 render it faithfully; the lie is upstream). messenger/qa have core_groups=null (all groups) so their flagging has a different, unverified cause (possibly genuine MCP unreachability from the api container, possibly the same tool-call failure) — needs triage, but the switchboard case alone establishes the misclassification. Note spend reads costs via per-butler MCP tool calls at all — the only fan-out family still doing so; every other honest fan-out queries DB pools directly.

findings.title: /spend/by-schedule splits each schedule into per-model rows — misranks 'which schedule is burning money' and creates duplicate React keys
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/sessions.py:780-813: schedule_costs GROUPs BY (st.name, st.cron, s.model). spend.py:_get_butler_schedule_costs (:970-1000) builds one ScheduleCost per row but drops the model field, so the API returns N indistinguishable rows per schedule. Live: 302 rows with ≥10 duplicate (schedule_name, butler) pairs, e.g. drain-curriculum-request/education appears twice ($2565.24/mo and $1147.51/mo projected). SpendPage.tsx:849 keys rows on `${s.butler}-${s.schedule_name}` → duplicate React keys.
findings.detail: The section's stated purpose (SpendPage.tsx:808: 'which schedule is burning money') is answered wrongly for any schedule that ran under 2+ models: its true burn (~$3712/mo for drain-curriculum-request) is split across rows and each fragment ranks lower than the schedule actually does. Duplicate keys also risk React reconciliation glitches on sort/update. Not in any known ledger — bu-h3ej9 only added the footnote to this table and did not touch the row shape; the model split predates it (pricing needs per-model rows internally, but they must be re-aggregated before ranking).

findings.title: FE flag-consumption registry has no reverse-completeness check — 14 shipped degraded flags sit outside the CI guard
findings.evidence: frontend/src/api/types.degraded-flags.test.ts REGISTRY lists 15 flags; grep of types.ts for degraded-shaped fields (*_source_error, *_available, *_unavailable, *_degraded) finds ~14 more not registered: balance_source_error, trends_source_error, rollups_source_error, heartbeat_source_error, heartbeat_unavailable, who_you_were_with_source_error, companion_names_unavailable, decisions_available, drift_check_available, device_liveness_available, health_available, hourly_events_available, parse_available, aggregates_available. No test asserts registry coverage of the flag population — only that registered entries have consumers.
findings.detail: All 14 currently have ≥1 real consumer (verified per-flag via grep excluding types.ts and tests), so nothing is broken today. But the registry's guarantee ('an emitted flag nobody reads fails CI') only holds for flags someone remembered to register — the chronicler/board/decisions flag families, several shipped in the same 48h window, were all forgotten. A consumer deleted in a refactor regresses silently. One suffix-sweep assertion (registry membership or explicit exemption) closes the loophole permanently.

moves.title: Classify tool-not-found as legitimately-absent in spend MCP fan-outs (or move spend off MCP onto direct DB reads)
moves.why: Kills the permanent switchboard false alarm on every /spend surface. Minimal fix: in spend.py's _get_butler_* helpers, treat FastMCP 'unknown tool' errors as absent-not-degraded (mirror memory.py::_is_missing_memory_schema_error) and only tracker.mark on unreachable/timeout; then triage why messenger/qa (all core groups enabled) still fail. Ideal fix: spend queries sessions/scheduled_tasks tables via db pools like every other honest fan-out, removing the MCP dependency and the core_groups coupling entirely.

moves.title: Re-aggregate /spend/by-schedule rows across models before ranking
moves.why: Restores the section's core answer ('which schedule is burning money'): sum cost/runs per (butler, schedule_name) after per-model pricing, keeping avg/run = total/total; fixes live-confirmed duplicate rows, wrong ranking, and duplicate React keys at SpendPage.tsx:849. Optionally expose the per-model split in a row drawer.

moves.title: Add reverse-completeness sweep to types.degraded-flags.test.ts
moves.why: One new assertion: scan types.ts for fields matching /(source_error|_available|_unavailable|_degraded|pools_failed)\b/ suffix shapes and fail if any is neither in REGISTRY nor in an explicit EXEMPT list (for non-flag lookalikes like replay_failed status literals and count fields like prs_failed). Converts the registry from opt-in to closed-world, which is the property bu-tpudw.5 intended.

findings.title: Drift sentinel cannot detect the failure mode that spawned it: a stale deployed image reports in-sync
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/deploy_drift.py:14-25 — 'codebase head' = alembic/versions on the running process's disk (get_chain_head), compared against per-schema alembic_version; the 'deployed SHA' third leg named in the bead title is explicitly scoped out (module docstring lines 19-25). In the original bu-zhfd0 incident the deployed image was pre-core_155, so its on-disk chains matched the stale DB — this sentinel would have reported is_drifted=false. The dashboard-api container mounts src/ but NOT alembic/ (docker inspect: mounts = src, roster, pyproject.toml, logs), so chains come from the image bake and go stale with it.
findings.detail: The sentinel covers 'image has migrations the DB lacks' (compose one-shot silently skipped) but not 'main has migrations the image lacks'. Both halves of bu-zhfd0's incident narrative need coverage: either the sentinel compares deployed GIT_SHA/migration heads against origin/main (a CI-side or fetching comparator), or the /system page renders a 'serving sha X, behind main by N' clause from the deployments ledger.

findings.title: Deployments ledger last mile missing: /api/system/deployments has zero frontend consumers and records an arbitrary migration head

Recorder: src/butlers/core/deployments.py:53 `SELECT version_num FROM "{schema}".alembic_version LIMIT 1` picks an arbitrary row of a multi-chain version table — live row shows migration_head="mem_007" (a memory-chain head) while the core chain is at core_165, so the ledger cannot answer 'which core migration is deployed'.
findings.detail: Endpoint is real and live (one honest row, GIT_SHA threaded from the image build), but the mechanism-real/last-mile-missing shape applies: nothing renders it, and the one representative head it snapshots is the least useful chain. Record the core head explicitly (or a per-chain map) and add a small Deployment card next to DriftTile/BackupTile on /system.

findings.title: secrets_lifecycle notifications can NEVER deliver: job runs in dashboard-api container but deliver() targets messenger MCP at localhost:41104 (container-relative loopback)
findings.detail: run_secrets_lifecycle_loop is started inside the dashboard-api process (src/butlers/api/app.py:268), and per its own docstring it composes the in-process deliver() dispatch path (src/butlers/jobs/secrets_lifecycle.py:54). deliver()/route() resolves the telegram module owner (messenger, port 41104 per roster/messenger/butler.toml:3) to a loopback MCP URL that is only valid inside the butlers-up container. Result in production DB: origin_butler=secrets_lifecycle_check has 164 attention_ledger rows in 7 days, 0 delivered — 143 suppressed (quiet_hours) + 21 deferred with reason 'delivery_error:ConnectionError: Failed to call tool telegram_send_message on http://localhost:41104/mcp: Client failed to connect'. Every awake-hours attempt on 07-11 (hours 04-14 UTC, post-deploy of bu-tdd4k.2's silent-branch ledger writes) failed identically, while 'general' butler deliveries from inside butlers-up succeeded at the same hours (06:07Z, 07:15Z delivered) — proving messenger was up and the failure is the caller's container, not telegram. A broken SPOTIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN has been silently un-notified for 7+ days. The new Trust Console panel correctly flags secrets_lifecycle_check red (suppressed_never_delivered) — the honesty mechanism works; the underlying delivery path is structurally dead. This is the api→daemon inverse of in-flight bu-01r64 (daemon→api event transport) and is not claimed by it.
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/attention/ledger/summary → {origin_butler: secrets_lifecycle_check, delivered: 0, suppressed: 143, deferred: 21, suppressed_never_delivered: true}; ledger row reason 'delivery_error:...localhost:41104/mcp...connection attempts failed'. Source: src/butlers/api/app.py:268 (loop runs in API app), src/butlers/jobs/secrets_lifecycle.py:42-56 (in-process deliver, no MCP client), roster/messenger/butler.toml:3 (port 41104).

findings.title: /api/decisions can never show data in the containerized deployment: dashboard-api services do not mount .beads/issues.export.jsonl, and snapshot-worktree deploys lack the file entirely

The JSONL bridge assumes compose runs from the main checkout; the actual deploy topology is snapshot worktrees.
findings.evidence: docker-compose.yml services parse: dashboard-api volumes=['./roster:/app/roster:ro','./logs:/app/logs','wa_bridge_socket:/tmp/wa-bridge','butlers_backups:/backups:ro'] (no beads mount); butlers-up:602 and butlers-up-hotreload:733 are the only issues.export.jsonl mounts. ls of /home/tze/gt/butlers/.worktrees/compose-latest-integration-20260711/.beads/ shows no issues.export.jsonl. src/butlers/api/routers/decisions.py:48 calls compute_decision_digest() in-process.

findings.title: Owner ingress via the dashboard chat widget never counts as owner engagement: 'dashboard' channel is unresolvable in the bu-tdd4k.5 engagement gate
findings.detail: The pipeline engagement gate (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:1857-1867) calls resolve_contact_by_channel(source, sender_value); for dashboard chat-widget messages source='dashboard' and sender='dashboard:operator' (live message_inbox row 2026-07-10 17:28Z: source_sender_identity='dashboard:operator'). The disengagement ratchet (check_total_disengagement_auto_off, a vision success marker) can therefore auto-disable proactive insights while the owner is actively using the console daily, and attention_daily_rollup.owner_ingress_count undercounts the owner's richest channel. findings.evidence: src/butlers/identity.py:129 (_CHANNEL_TYPE_TO_PREDICATE has no 'dashboard' key); src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:1860-1867 (is_owner_ingress requires resolve_contact_by_channel match); live DB: message_inbox dashboard row sender='dashboard:operator', attention_daily_rollup = 0 rows.

landings.evidence: roster/switchboard/butler.toml carries both schedules: decision-review-digest (cron '0 9 * * 1') and decision-escalation-check (every 6h, 48h threshold); jobs registered in src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py:1710-1711 delegating to src/butlers/jobs/decision_review.py (run_decision_review_digest / run_decision_escalation_check); tests/jobs/test_decision_review.py exists. findings.title: Nightly faketime leg hangs at 99% and dies at GitHub's 6h default kill — the time-bomb signal it exists to produce is silently lost
findings.evidence: Run 29140308642 (first scheduled run after PR #3131 merged): jobs faketime-matrix(+45d) and (+120d) both started 04:52:49Z, pytest reached [ 99%] by 05:14:11Z with >=3 'F' failures visible in the +45d progress dots (log lines 05:13:30 and 05:14:01), then produced no further output until step cancelled at 10:53:02Z (##[error]The operation was canceled; orphan pytest/python pids reaped). .github/workflows/nightly.yml:53-142 has no timeout-minutes and no per-test timeout, so the hang consumed the 6h job limit on BOTH matrix legs (~12h runner time), pytest never printed its failure summary (run with -q --tb=short, names only at end), and the run conclusion is 'cancelled' — not 'failure' — so the workflow's own documented alerting premise (nightly.yml:74-78: 'failure here is visible via GitHub's built-in scheduled-workflow-failure email') never fires. Net: the leg PROVED there are >=3 live wall-clock time-bombs detonating within +45d, but nobody can see which tests they are, and every subsequent nightly will repeat the burn.
findings.detail: Two distinct defects: (1) a deterministic hang under faketime somewhere in the last ~1% of the suite (both offsets hang, so it is systematic, likely a wall-clock-derived deadline that faketime pushes 45/120 days out); (2) no failure-surfacing when the job dies by limit — cancelled conclusion suppresses both the pytest summary and the scheduled-failure notification, converting a found-signal into silence. This is exactly the 'mechanism real, last mile missing' shape: the detector works, the reporting channel is dead.

findings.title: Parallel-migration revision collision DID recur during this fleet run (core_164 twice); the new guard is post-merge detection only — nothing prevents the second merge
findings.evidence: PR #3135 (merged 2026-07-11T04:47Z) root-cause section: 'PR #3125 and PR #3127 were developed in parallel from the same core_163 head. Both independently introduced revision core_164 and merged without a textual conflict.' The fix renumbered to core_165 and added a global revision-uniqueness guard (tests/config/test_migration_chain_head.py: _collect_revision_locations walks every chain via AST, catches typed assignments and cross-chain collisions; 9 tests pass locally). But the guard runs in the same CI that is (a) not a required check (main is unprotected by design) and (b) evaluated on each PR's merge-ref at the time CI ran — the second PR's green predates the first PR's merge and is never re-run, so the identical race merges clean again next time two workers each take core_N+1 off the same head.
findings.detail: This is the second occurrence of the exact hazard in the cross-repo memory ledger (first: earlier fleet run). The guard upgrades the failure from 'confusing red on every open PR' to 'one precise duplicate-revision assertion', which is real value, but detection-after-merge still costs a main-red window plus a manual renumber/rechain PR each time. Prevention needs a pre-merge step that re-validates against FRESH origin/main (coordinator/reviewer protocol: re-run test_migration_chain_head.py on a rebase of origin/main immediately before merging any migration-bearing PR), or serializing migration-bearing beads to one in flight (some epics already carry 'only child .1 may add a migration' — that convention is not fleet-wide).

findings.title: ButlerFinanceFinancesTab computes the monthly-spend window from a HOST-local month start — missed by the bu-5fwbh owner-tz sweep's follow-up beads
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerFinanceFinancesTab.tsx:593-600: monthStart = formatInTimeZone(new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), 1), OWNER_TZ_DEFAULT, 'yyyy-MM-dd') — getFullYear/getMonth read the HOST clock, so on the 1st of a month in owner tz while the host is still in the previous month (any viewer/host behind Asia/Singapore around month rollover), the KPI window becomes the entire previous month + 1 day. The bu-5fwbh sweep (PR #3062) filed 6 follow-ups; the only remaining open one, bu-z0fn1, covers DateEyebrow only — this site is uncatalogued. lib/day-window.ts (bu-s0d8j) is the designated shared primitive and is unused here.
findings.detail: Same 'low impact for single-owner deployment' class as bu-z0fn1 (owner's browser tz == owner tz in practice), but it is a data-window bug, not a display bug, so it belongs in the sweep's ledger. qa/utils.ts:28-38 and CaseDossierHeader.tsx:27 also use host-local getFullYear but only for same-year display formatting (benign).

landings.item: PR #3135 — fix duplicate core migration revision + global uniqueness guard
landings.evidence: Merged 07-11T04:47Z: core_164 kept for breaker-resets, attention-daily-rollup renumbered core_165; tests/config/test_migration_chain_head.py gained an AST-walking global revision-uniqueness guard across all chains (typed assignments + cross-chain collisions; verified passing locally). moves.title: Bound the faketime-matrix job: timeout-minutes ~90 + pytest-timeout per-test so hangs surface as NAMED failures
moves.why: The leg's entire purpose is producing a signal, and its first run proved it detects real +45d time-bombs (>=3 F's) then destroyed the evidence by hanging to the 6h kill — no summary, conclusion 'cancelled' (which does not read as a scheduled-workflow failure), ~12h runner burn per night, repeating every night until fixed. Adding timeout-minutes plus pytest-timeout (thread method) converts the hang into a failing run that names both the hung test and the 3 latent time-bombs.

moves.title: Pre-merge freshness check for migration-bearing PRs: re-run the revision-uniqueness guard against current origin/main immediately before merge (coordinator/reviewer protocol clause), or serialize migration PRs fleet-wide
moves.why: The core_164 collision recurred within one fleet run because two parallel workers allocated the same next revision and the second merged on a stale green; the new guard only fires after the damage. A one-line protocol step ('before merging any PR touching alembic/versions/, fetch origin/main and run tests/config/test_migration_chain_head.py on the merge result') closes the race at S cost without branch protection, consistent with the unprotected-main doctrine.

For 'unknown' rows the dot goes amber via sourcesPartiallyDegraded but the count text still includes unknowable rows in N/N.
findings.detail: Two verdicts on the same payload, inches apart, and the five-second one (the pill) is the lenient one. Violates 'one fact, many numbers' (#8) and 'failure never impersonates health' (#1): a butler silent for 3 days against a daily cadence is exactly what the pill exists to catch. Live-confirmed the payload carries aggregates.overdue (currently 0) and that the pill's inputs come from the same response.

findings.title: Owner Pause is stored and rendered as a quarantine emergency with a NULL reason
findings.evidence: ButlerDetailActions.tsx:143-149 Pause sends state='quarantined' via setButlerEligibility, whose request body carries ONLY eligibility_state (client.ts:2501-2512, SetEligibilityRequest has no reason field). Backend handler roster/switchboard/api/router.py:729-748: when quarantining, quarantined_at=now but quarantine_reason=update_fields.get('quarantine_reason')=None. The board then renders the paused butler with a destructive-red rail (StatusBoardCell.tsx:111), a red QUARANTINED chip, and a needs-you strip entry whose reasonFor() falls back to the bare word 'quarantined' (NeedsYouStrip.tsx:35). The detail page's own quarantine-info span (ButlerDetailActions.tsx:240-255) shows 'Quarantined <time>' with no reason.
findings.detail: A deliberate owner action fabricates a fleet emergency indistinguishable from a healing/automated quarantine — the inverse of fabricated calm: fabricated alarm. It also destroys the restore decision's provenance: an operator later deciding whether Resume is safe sees a reason-less quarantine and cannot tell 'I paused this on purpose' from 'healing killed it'. The state model needs an owner-pause vocabulary (or at minimum a written reason like 'Paused by owner from dashboard') and a non-destructive PAUSED render.

findings.title: Pause/Resume mutation fails silently and lacks the undo pattern its sibling restore control earned
findings.evidence: handlePauseToggle (ButlerDetailActions.tsx:143-149) calls setEligibility.mutate with no onSuccess/onError callbacks, and useSetEligibility itself (use-general.ts:51-61) defines no onError — a failed pause resets the button label to 'Pause' with zero user-visible signal. Contrast ButlersPage restore, which schedules through a 5s undo window with success/error toasts (ButlersPage.tsx:133-162). Pausing (quarantining) a butler is at least as consequential as restoring one, yet fires instantly with no confirm, no undo, and no failure feedback.
findings.detail: Earned-calm violation on the failure path: the owner cannot distinguish 'paused' from 'pause request dropped' without re-checking the registry. Same mutation also only invalidates ['switchboard-registry'] (standing known — board cell staleness), so even a successful pause leaves the board contradicting the button for up to 5 minutes.

findings.title: Overview 'per session' cost quotient mixes two time windows into a number that is neither
findings.evidence: ButlerOverviewTab.tsx:319 renders `${formatCurrency(sessions24h > 0 ? costToday / sessions24h : 0)} / session` where costToday is the owner-tz calendar-day spend from /api/spend summary (line 270, live-verified shape) and sessions24h is the rolling-24h board count (line 269). At 9am the quotient divides 9 hours of spend by 24 hours of sessions.
findings.detail: One-fact-many-numbers family (#8): the displayed derived value is computed from two sources with different windows. Either divide today's spend by today's session count (total_sessions is already in the spend summary payload, scoped per butler via the by_butler map's sibling data) or label it honestly. Note the two SPEND sources themselves currently agree (board cost_today 0.54872363 for general == spend summary by_butler.general, live-confirmed), so only the quotient is wrong.

audits.ideal: The roster is the fleet's five-second verification instrument: one composed verdict, spoken identically by every clause. The header pill says "2 need you" exactly when the triage strip lists two rows — overdue and unknown never counted as healthy — and the footer band carries the same OVERDUE/UNKNOWN cells the strip derives from. A butler the owner paused reads PAUSED in neutral/amber with the owner's own reason ("paused by owner, 2h ago"), never impersonating a healing quarantine; a real quarantine always carries its cause. Every clause is a door that lands on its evidence: a pending approval opens its own dossier at /approvals/:id, an hour bar opens that hour's sessions (already true), a quarantine reason opens the eligibility-history trail. Every consequential control acknowledges within 100ms, offers a symmetric undo window (pause and restore alike), reports failure loudly, and the board cell reflects the change on the next paint, not the next 5-minute reconcile. The detail Overview renders only numbers the system can prove, derived from the same board payload as the grid — no parallel status vocabulary, no ?? 0 spend, no fabricated flat stripe — with degraded sources named inline. j/k+Enter triage over cells and strip rows (deferred keyboard batch) closes the loop hands-on-keys.

Array(24).fill(0) fallbacks), 312-322 (spend panel + per-session quotient), use-butler-status-board.ts row.activity/cellTone/hourlyStripeError (the honest fields already exist), spend summary total_sessions for a same-window quotient.

findings.title: From/To date filters silently drop the named day (UTC-midnight, exclusive-To) — calm empty state fabricated from a filter-semantics bug
findings.evidence: Live-confirmed: GET /api/sessions/aggregate?from_date=2026-07-11&to_date=2026-07-11 returns total=0 while from_date=2026-07-11&to_date=2026-07-12 returns total=97 — the natural 'show me just that day' gesture (From=To on the page's type="date" inputs, SessionsPage.tsx:480-504) matches zero sessions because to_date binds as midnight at the START of the To day and _build_where uses started_at <= to_date (sessions.py:139-141; client.ts:668-670 maps since/until → from_date/to_date verbatim). The table then renders the calm EmptyState 'No sessions found.' (SessionTable.tsx:111-119) and the KPI strip shows honest-looking zeros labeled 'Matching filters' (SessionsKpiStrip.tsx). Compounding: boundaries are UTC midnight, not owner-timezone — contradicting the landed owner-timezone sweep convention (bu-jlzxf et al., lib/day-window helper exists) — so even a correct exclusive-end fix would still clip the owner's day by the UTC offset.
findings.detail: This is sin #2 (an interpretation error impersonating an empty state) on the page's only time-scoping control. Every consumer of the filter params inherits it identically: the list, the window-true KPI strip, and the stripe chart all show a coherent, mutually-corroborating zero for a day that had 97 sessions — coherence makes the falsehood more convincing, not less. Fix is small: interpret From as owner-tz start-of-day and To as owner-tz end-of-day inclusive (exclusive next-midnight), via the existing frontend day-window helper, with a contract test asserting From=To=<day> returns that day's sessions.

findings.title: Sessions LIST fan-out degraded flag has zero pixel readers — table, pinned strip, and stripe chart render a partial fleet as complete
findings.evidence: Backend emits KeysetMeta.sources_degraded on every GET /api/sessions page (sessions.py:375-383; typed at frontend types.ts:58-69). No non-test frontend code reads it: SessionsPage.tsx:155-158 destructures only has_more/next_cursor; the pinned strip consumes only whole-query isError booleans (SessionsPinnedStrip.tsx:131-134 via SessionsPage.tsx:524-525), not partial fan-out degradation on its running/recent-failures list queries; the stripe chart passes meta through untouched (session-stripe-utils.ts:193) and renders 'No sessions in the selected window' (SessionStripeChart.tsx:152-160) with no degraded branch. The bu-tpudw.5 registry test passes anyway because consumption is checked per flag-NAME codebase-wide (types.degraded-flags.test.ts:70 'sessions list/aggregate, search, issues, approvals' is one entry) — the aggregate consumers (SessionsKpiStrip.tsx:59-82, SessionsVerdictOpener.tsx:68-73) satisfy it for the list too.
findings.detail: Sin #6 + #7 in one: the honesty flag shipped backend-first on the list endpoint with no pixels, and the shared gate (flag-consumption registry) froze at a granularity that exempts exactly this case. Concrete failure: one butler pool down → the chronological table shows other pools' rows as a seamless complete history; filter Butler=<down pool> → rows=[], sources_degraded=[pool], and the table renders the calm 'No sessions found.' empty state. The page becomes internally contradictory: the verdict opener and KPI strip (aggregate path, bu-tpudw.2) correctly name the degraded pool at the top while the table below it asserts a clean empty — two truths about one window. Fix: read meta.sources_degraded in SessionsPage for the main list + both pinned queries + stripe data, gate the EmptyState on it (SourceDegradedNote instead of 'No sessions found'), and sharpen the registry test to per-endpoint-consumer granularity so the next beachhead can't freeze.

findings.title: Session-detail evidence computed and shipped but dropped at the FE type boundary: correction_count and process_log retry lineage
findings.evidence: Backend SessionDetail carries correction_count (models/session.py:178), populated by a real per-request COUNT(*) against corrections (sessions.py:275-282), and ProcessLog ships retry_attempted/retry_succeeded/result_source/attempt_count (selected sessions.py:259-261; written live by spawner.py:1884,2060). The FE SessionDetail type omits all five fields (types.ts:240-270 — process_log stops at runtime_type/created_at/expires_at) and zero non-test consumers exist. Meanwhile SessionDossier.tsx:15-19 claims 'Renders EVERY SessionDetail field the store holds' as its design contract.
findings.detail: Two costs: (1) failure triage stops one hop short of the evidence — a failed session's Root Evidence section (SessionDossier.tsx:292-306) shows exit_code/stderr but not whether that stderr came from attempt 1 of 2, whether a retry was attempted or succeeded, or the result_source; (2) zero-cruft violation — the backend pays a corrections COUNT(*) on every detail fetch (including the pinned strip's useSessionErrorExcerpts batch, which fires it once per pinned failure) for a number no pixel ever shows. Either render (attempt-lineage row in Root Evidence, correction count chip) or delete the computation. The dossier's 'every field' comment is currently false and will silently rot further.

findings.title: One dossier, two failure dialects: SessionDetailPage lacks the drawer's named pool-down (503) and not-found states
findings.evidence: SessionDetailDrawer.tsx:52-75 branches on ApiError.status === 503 to render a distinct role=alert 'Session detail unavailable' state naming the down pool (bu-tpudw.2). SessionDetailPage.tsx:36-45 — the full-page route that 10+ surfaces deep-link into — folds every failure into the generic Page error card (error={isError || notFound ? (error ?? new Error("Session not found")) : null}). The text stays honest only because ApiError.message carries the FastAPI detail string (client.ts:579-581), but the 503-vs-404 distinction, alert semantics, and testid the drawer earned do not exist on the page.
findings.detail: bu-qvnce.5 unified the dossier body (SessionDossier shared by both) but the failure states forked: the drawer got the honest tri-state, the page kept the generic card. A deep link from a notification to a session in a down pool reads as a generic error page rather than the named, retry-worthy 'pool unreachable — may exist' state. Extract the drawer's error branching into the shared component.

audits.jarvis_gap: The page now opens with a window-true verdict, pins live/failed work, roves with j/k/[/]/y, and names degraded aggregates — but its truth layer is still perimeter-only: the chronological table and chart (the surfaces the eye actually trusts) can render a partial fleet or a mis-windowed day as calm, complete history, and the dossier stops one hop short of retry-lineage evidence on failures.
audits.movement_claim: improved — bu-tpudw.2 verified in the pixels: 404-vs-503 split live-confirmed (bogus id → 404 'Session not found'; 503 branch with pool-naming detail at sessions.py:518-529), drawer resolves globally with a named role=alert pool-down state (SessionDetailDrawer.tsx:52-75), and aggregate meta.sources_degraded is consumed by both the KPI strip (SessionsKpiStrip.tsx:59-82, live meta:{} on healthy fleet) and the verdict opener's all-clear suppression (SessionsVerdictOpener.tsx:68-73)
audits.ideal: The ideal /sessions is the fleet's flight recorder with a five-second verdict: it opens on a window-true, degradation-aware verdict line (already real), and every layer below it tells the same truth — the table, chart, and pinned strips inherit the exact same degraded-source vocabulary as the opener, so a down pool reads as 'pool X unreachable' in every place its rows would have appeared, never as an empty day. Time scoping speaks the owner's clock: From=To=yesterday means the owner's yesterday, inclusive, everywhere (list, KPIs, chart) via one shared day-window primitive. The dossier is a closed evidence loop: metadata → prompt → tool-call timeline (live-tailing while running, known-deferred) → result/error with full attempt lineage (attempt N of M, retry outcome, result source, exit code, stderr) → corrections count → trace/request/parent doors, identical whether reached as a drawer, a deep-linked page, or a keyboard hop, with identical named failure states when the session can't be resolved. Nothing rendered is computed and dropped; nothing dropped is still computed.

moves.why: The drawer earned named 503 pool-down / 404 not-found states in bu-tpudw.2 but the deep-linked full page — the target of 10+ inbound surfaces — still folds everything into a generic error card, so the same failed resolution speaks two dialects.

findings.title: Fleet chronicle's primary summary column leaks machine envelopes (<user_message> fences, QA system prompts, skill preambles)
findings.evidence: Live GET /api/timeline?limit=50: 30/50 head-page summaries are machine text — 9 contain raw XML fences (e.g. '<user_message>Came online</user_message>', 'The user reports: <user_message>Status changed to away</user_message> This appea…'), 1 renders a QA canary's system prompt ('You are a QA investigation agent for the butler system. An automated patrol cycl…' shown as an error row for travel), 3 show transcript headers ('=== Chat: The Masses of Massachuset's (id: -1001323592475) ='), 20 are '/message-triage' skill preambles (mostly collapsed as heartbeats). Mechanism: src/butlers/api/routers/timeline.py:65-99,110-145 — _derive_session_summary unwraps only <routed_message> and strips 5 fixed preamble markers; <user_message> fences, 'Please use the /X skill' preambles, and QA-canary system prompts pass through verbatim into the serif summary column that is the row's main content. No open bead covers this (bd title search).
findings.detail: This is the one column the owner actually reads on the chronicle. The header promises 'Every household event, newest first' in human terms; a third of the page is prompt plumbing. Fix is small and server-side: generalize the fence-unwrap regex to <user_message> (and any single top-level XML fence), strip 'Please use the /<skill> skill' preambles to a trigger label, and label QA canary sessions ('QA patrol investigation') via trigger_source/prompt prefix instead of dumping the system prompt.

findings.title: Failed notification deliveries render calm at row level and are invisible to the 'Errors only' lens
findings.evidence: Live GET /api/timeline?event_type=notification: 5 consecutive events with data.status='failed' (telegram to owner, 'Credential SPOTIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN has expired', repeating every ~30min — an owner-notification chain that has been bouncing for hours). Row rendering (frontend/src/components/timeline/TimelineLedger.tsx:53-66) gives every notification the same neutral purple dot; delivery status appears only inside the drawer (TimelineEventDrawer.tsx:110-111). The 'Errors only' built-in view sets event_type=['error'] (TimelinePage.tsx:68), which the backend maps solely to sessions with success=False (timeline.py:155,261-274) — bounced notifications are excluded, so a fleet whose every owner alert is failing shows a clean Errors view.
findings.detail: NEW strengthening evidence for the deferred errors-lens move: this is failure impersonating health on the honesty surface itself, demonstrated live with a real multi-hour owner-notification outage. Minimum fix independent of the full errors-lens: destructive dot + 'failed' word on notification rows with status='failed', and fold delivery failures into the Errors built-in view's semantics.

findings.title: User-action failures on the timeline die in console.error — no pixels
findings.evidence: (a) 'Load older' failure: use-timeline-ledger.ts:122-125 catches and console.errors; button re-enables with no visible feedback — walkthrough 'Repetition' fails (user clicks again, nothing explains why). (b) Save-view failure: TimelinePage.tsx:177-179 console.error, dialog stays open with no error text. (c) Delete saved view: TimelinePage.tsx:274 fires deleteSavedView.mutate with no confirm, no undo, and the hook (use-timeline-saved-views.ts:96-104) has no onError — a one-click permanent destructive action whose failure is also fully silent. (d) Custom saved-views list drops isError: TimelinePage.tsx:130 `customViewsResp?.data ?? []` — a saved-views backend failure renders as 'you have no custom views' (errors-impersonating-calm instance the bu-jad4j/bu-tpudw batches did not cover).
findings.detail: Four instances of the same sin cluster on one page: sin (2) on the views list, design-bar 'Recovery' (destructive without undo/confirm) on delete, and unacknowledged failures on Load older / Save. Delete-active-view also strands ?view=<deleted-id> in the URL with filters silently retained and no highlighted chip.

findings.title: 'This page' heartbeat rollup describes the live head page, not what's rendered; new-events pill counts telemetry ticks
findings.evidence: use-timeline-ledger.ts:149 returns heartbeatRollup from head.data.meta (always the live head page, computed backend-side over page[:limit] at timeline.py:338-343); TimelinePage.tsx:231-241 renders it as 'This page: N ticks…' even while unpinned, when the rendered list is the committed snapshot + older pages (use-timeline-ledger.ts:102) — the label and the rows disagree about which page 'this page' is. Separately, newCount (use-timeline-ledger.ts:97-100) counts all head events not in the committed set, including is_heartbeat ticks, so during history review the 'N new events' pill inflates with switchboard classification telemetry (live head page: 3 of 50 events were heartbeats; ratio is higher in active hours — 20/50 skill-triage events carry is_heartbeat=True).
findings.detail: One-fact-two-scopes mismatch (taxonomy sin 8, mild). Both fixable client-side: derive the rollup from the rendered `events` array (HeartbeatGroupRow already computes per-group honest counts from members), and either exclude heartbeats from newCount or split the pill copy ('N events · M ticks').

audits.jarvis_gap: The chronicle's skeleton is genuinely JARVIS-grade — honest cursor pagination with composite keyset, per-source degraded_sources consumed as a named banner, a live badge with a true 'Down' state (bu-qvnce.2 verified wired at use-timeline-ledger.ts:141/TimelinePage.tsx:217), URL-backed shareable filters, off-page ?event= resolved honestly (EventNotFoundNotice), and drawer focus choreography. What keeps it from world-class is that the content and the failure semantics haven't caught up with the plumbing: the primary summary column shows prompt-envelope machine text for a third of rows, a live multi-hour owner-notification delivery outage renders as calm purple rows that the 'Errors only' lens cannot see, and every user-action failure path (load older, save/delete view) dies in the console. Five-second verification of 'what happened and what failed' is not yet achievable from this page alone — the owner must open drawers to discover bounced deliveries and mentally decode XML fences to read intent.
audits.ideal: The ideal /timeline opens to a human-readable narrative of the household's last hours: every row's summary is genuine intent ('Came online', 'Spotify listening session: 9 tracks', 'Alert to you BOUNCED — Spotify credential expired'), with all machine envelopes unwrapped server-side and QA canaries labeled as patrols. Failure is legible at row level: failed sessions and bounced notification deliveries both carry the destructive mark and both land in an honest Errors lens, so an owner whose alert channel is down sees it in the first five seconds, not after opening a drawer. Paging into history freezes the view with a truthful new-events count that excludes telemetry ticks; the heartbeat rollup describes exactly the rows on screen. Every row is one keystroke from root evidence (j/k + Enter drawer, o to the session transcript or the specific notification record), saved views are scoped to this surface, and every mutation either confirms, undoes, or shows its failure as pixels.
audits.movement_claim: unchanged — no timeline-specific work landed in the 07-10..07-12 window (the batch commits touched other surfaces); the previously-landed honesty mechanisms (Down badge, URL-backed filters, off-page ?event= notice) were verified intact, and the two new major findings are newly-surfaced pre-existing defects, not regressions.

moves.title: Unwrap <user_message> fences, skill preambles, and QA-canary prompts in _derive_session_summary
moves.why: The chronicle's primary column is machine text for ~30/50 live head-page rows; readable intent is the whole point of a chronicle and this is the highest friction-x-frequency defect on the surface.

findings.title: Optimistic ack is visually inert: mutation patches status, UI renders effective_status
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:72-73 and :86-87 — updateItems maps {...n, status: "read"} only; frontend/src/components/notifications/notification-feed.tsx:180 renders displayStatus = n.effective_status ?? n.status; effective_status is non-optional (frontend/src/api/types.ts:331) and the backend list query always populates it via CASE ... ELSE status (src/butlers/api/routers/notifications.py:210-217), so it is never nullish and the optimistic flip never reaches the screen. Same gating at NotificationsPage.tsx:250 keeps the 'a' act key and Mark-read/Dismiss buttons alive during the window.
findings.detail: Mark-read and Acknowledge-all are classified OPTIMISTIC per the shared primitive's doctrine (use-optimistic-mutation.ts module doc: 'the owner should never see a spinner for these'), but the row badge stays Failed and triage controls stay active until the invalidation refetch lands — the entire optimistic mechanism is dead weight on this surface. Fix is one line per updateItems: also set effective_status: "read".

findings.title: Hard stats-request error renders green 0.0% failure-rate all-clear under a verdict that reports the outage

Contrast: the verdict opener on the SAME page consumes isError (NotificationsPage.tsx:146-150), and DashboardPage.tsx:136-137 consumes isError for the SAME hook.
findings.detail: New instance of sin #2 (error impersonating calm) that bu-jad4j.2 did not cover — that bead handled only the 200-with-source_available=false path. Also failedCount = statsResponse?.data?.failed ?? 0 (NotificationsPage.tsx:275) silently hides the Acknowledge-all button on error.

findings.title: Acknowledging a failure rewrites history: status='read' overwrites 'failed', retro-greening the Failure Rate; ack-all is filter-blind
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/notifications.py:512-521 (UPDATE notifications SET status = 'read' WHERE id = $1) and :588-590 (UPDATE notifications SET status = 'read' WHERE status = 'failed'); no acknowledged_at/read_at column — the row's failed status is destroyed, so stats Q3 (terminal failures) and the Failure Rate tile (failed/total, notification-stats-bar.tsx:39) drop to green 0.0% after ack even though 33 deliveries genuinely failed (live: stats.failed=33 today). POST /ack-failed takes no filter/window params while the button (NotificationsPage.tsx:283-294) renders inside a filterable, windowed page.
findings.detail: Two honesty defects in one mechanism: (1) 'read' and 'was-failed-then-acknowledged' collapse into one indistinguishable state — triage mutates the historical failure record, violating 'nothing fabricated' in reverse (fabricated calm about the past); (2) an owner filtered to butler=finance who clicks 'Acknowledge all failed (33)' acks every butler's failures fleet-wide, including ones never displayed. The error text survives on the row but no stats or filter can find it again (status='read' rows with error set are the only trace).

findings.title: One live root cause renders as 21 identical, traceless failure rows — no incident grouping, no door to evidence
findings.evidence: Live GET /api/notifications?limit=5: five (of 21, per stats by_butler.switchboard=21) byte-identical rows — switchboard credential-expiry telegram failure repeating every 30min since 2026-07-11T13:22, each with session_id=null, trace_id=null, error='ConnectionError ... localhost:41104/mcp'. notification-feed.tsx:209-228 only renders doors when session_id/trace_id exist, so these rows have zero drill-down; the actionable URL in the message body ('http://localhost:41200/secrets?focus=s%3ASPOTIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN') renders as truncated plain text (notification-feed.tsx:203, truncate at 60 chars), not a link — and points at the prod port.
findings.detail: Sin #3 (drill-down dead end) plus a five-second-verification failure: the verdict correctly says '21 from switchboard' but the drill-down is 21 identical rows spanning multiple pages with no first-seen/last-seen, no count, and no path to the expired credential or the dead bridge. Daemon-originated (non-session) notifications structurally carry no trace spine at all.

findings.title: Three coexisting definitions of 'failed' plus two unlabeled time scopes on one screen
findings.evidence: stats.failed excludes retried (terminal-failure self-join, notifications.py:456-476); list ?status=failed uses raw equality including retried rows (notifications.py:180-183); POST /ack-failed updates raw status='failed' (notifications.py:588). Live today they coincide (retried total=0, both 33) but any supersession diverges tile count, tile-click list total, and ack count. Separately: the stats tiles are all-time with no scope label while the verdict opener directly above says 'in the last 24h' — live screen shows Failed=33 and '22 failed notifications in the last 24h' simultaneously with nothing explaining the difference.
findings.detail: Sin #8 (one fact, many numbers). The Failed tile is a filter anchor (bu-qvnce.13) that pivots to a predicate computed differently from the number on the tile; the Acknowledge-all button count (terminal failures) can undercount what the UPDATE actually acks (raw failed incl. retried).

audits.ideal: The ideal /notifications is a delivery-truth instrument, not a log: it opens with the existing windowed verdict, but beneath it repeated failures collapse into incidents — one row per (butler, channel, message, error-class) with count, first/last seen, and a mini-sparkline — so today's dead-telegram-bridge outage reads as "1 incident, 21 attempts, since 13:22, door: SPOTIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN expired → /secrets?focus=…" instead of pages of clones. Every row has a door: session/trace when spawned from a run, an origin/credential door when daemon-originated. Acknowledgment is its own dimension (acknowledged_at), never a rewrite of delivery truth — Failure Rate stays honest forever, and "read" rows still remember they failed; ack-all acknowledges exactly the visible predicate and reports the count it touched. There is exactly one definition of "failed" shared by the tile, the filter it pivots to, the verdict, and the ack mutation, each labeled with its window. All four tiles, the feed, and the verdict share one three-state honesty contract (loading / named-error / value) for both the source_available flag and hard request errors. Keyboard triage stays (j/k/a) and gains full-text reveal (Tip or row-expand on Enter) so truncated errors are reachable without a mouse. The optimistic ack actually flips the pixel it claims to.

findings.title: 349k poisoned audit rows (double-encoded metadata) 500-crash any audit page or occurrences drilldown that touches them
findings.evidence: DB (read-only): SELECT jsonb_typeof(metadata), count(*) FROM public.audit_log → string=349,113 of 1.207M rows, spanning 2026-06-14→2026-07-05 (write-path fixed since; top actors switchboard 342k, education 3.5k). Live: GET /api/audit-log?actor=memory&kind=privileged&limit=20 → VALIDATION_ERROR 'metadata Input should be a valid dictionary'; GET /api/audit-log?actor=dashboard&result=error&limit=20 → same; GET /api/issues/audit_error_group:runtimeerror-codex-cli-...-access-token-...::multiple/occurrences → HTTP 400 VALIDATION_ERROR (this is the TOP group in today's live feed). Mechanism: AuditLogEntry.metadata is dict-typed (src/butlers/api/models/audit.py:51) and from_record passes the raw value through (audit.py:83); rows written during the double-encode era (the anti-pattern documented in routers/audit.py:245-253, bu-qki26/bu-aaacv — fixed at write time only, never repaired) hold a JSONB string. FE renders AuditLogTable's ErrorState 'may be temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.' (AuditLogTable.tsx:154-161) — a deterministic data-poisoning failure impersonating a transient outage; typing 'memory' in the page's own Actor filter reproducibly kills the whole table.
findings.detail: Failure impersonating the wrong class (retry never helps) plus a 3-week hole in the audit ledger behind the dashboard's audit surface. Fix is two-sided: a one-shot repair migration normalizing jsonb_typeof='string' metadata (owner doctrine: prefer cruft cleanup over compat), plus a tolerant json.loads fallback in AuditLogEntry.from_record with a regression test so one bad row can never take out a whole page again.

findings.title: Occurrences drilldown re-derives groups ALL-TIME while the feed is windowed — issue_key drifts, live 404s, counts disagree, and the uncapped scan bu-qvnce.13 killed is back
findings.evidence: list_issue_occurrences (src/butlers/api/routers/issues.py:518) calls build_audit_group_query() with NO since bound and NO limit, then loops every group in Python to re-match issue_key. Live: 7d feed returns audit_error_group:http-400::switchboard (occ 24, butlers=[switchboard]); GET /api/issues/audit_error_group:http-400::switchboard/occurrences → 404 'No active issue group found' because all-time the same error groups as butlers=[dashboard,memory,switchboard] → butler='multiple' → different key. FE shows 'Could not load occurrences. Try again shortly.' (IssuesPanel.tsx:121-127) — permanent, retry-proof. Where the key doesn't drift, counts do: 24h feed 'Seen 4x' vs all-time meta.total 41 for the same group (one fact, many numbers), and the FE never shows the total or a load-more (IssuesPage.tsx:414 uses data only; 50-row default cap silent).
findings.detail: The signature drill-down of the Issues surface (Seen Nx → its N rows) is broken live for the two most prominent groups in today's feed (http-400 via key drift, token-refresh via poisoned rows). Fix: pass the feed's window through to the occurrences endpoint and reuse the same since+cap; match on error_summary rather than re-deriving a lossy key; render 'showing 50 of N' from meta.total.

findings.title: issue_key is not unique — 80-char slug truncation collapses distinct error groups into one key; ack/selection/drilldown cross-contaminate
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/issues?window=all returns TWO rows with the identical key 'audit_error_group:runtimeerror-codex-cli-exited-with-code-1-your-access-token-could-not-be-refresh::multiple' (occ 166, 9 butlers vs occ 2860, 10 butlers — distinct error summaries truncated to the same slug by _ISSUE_TYPE_MAX_LEN=80, audit_grouping.py:218-226; compute_issue_key = type::butler, models/__init__.py:254-269). Consequences in code: React key collision in IssuesPanel's map (IssuesPanel.tsx:372 key={issue.issue_key}), acknowledging one acks both (dismissed_issues keyed by issue_key, issues.py:373-378), j/k selection and occurrences matching hit whichever row comes first (issues.py:524-528 first-match loop). Corollary, same root: the key embeds window-dependent aggregates (butler set), so an ack recorded in the 7d view (…::switchboard) silently does not apply in the all-time view (…::multiple).
findings.detail: Group identity should be window-independent and collision-free: key audit groups on a hash of the full normalized error_summary alone (drop the butler-set component for audit groups). This also fixes cross-window ack stability and the occurrences 404 class in one move.

findings.title: ?result= is an active but invisible predicate on /audit-log — every Issues 'View' link narrows the ledger with no pixel and no in-UI clear
findings.evidence: Every audit-derived issue link carries result=error (audit_grouping.py:286-291); AuditLogPage forwards it to the API (AuditLogPage.tsx:61,93) but the deep-link chip row renders chips only for ?key= and ?actor= (AuditLogPage.tsx:160-198) and 'Clear filters' deletes only actor/action/since (lines 123-132). A user arriving from Issues sees a silently error-only feed with nothing naming the predicate and no way to remove it short of editing the URL. Compounding: the default privileged noise filter (kind=privileged, audit.py:405-407) excludes the very rows some groups count — the http-400 group's 24 occurrences are heartbeat POSTs excluded via the unescaped '_' wildcard in "NOT LIKE '%_heartbeat'" (live: result=error&actor=switchboard totals 1086 unfiltered vs 1048 privileged) — so 'Seen 24x → View' can land on a page containing none of its 24 rows, unexplained.
findings.detail: Hidden-filter sin: the surface asserts 'this is the audit log' while showing a doubly-narrowed slice. Fix: chip every non-default predicate (result, and a named note when the default noise filter is active on an error-pivot arrival), make Clear filters clear everything, and have issue View links opt out of the noise filter (?noise=all) when the group's rows are noise-classed.

findings.title: 'View in Issues' q-pivot can land on a false all-clear ('No issues recorded.')
findings.evidence: AuditLogTable.tsx:356-364 links /issues?q=<firstErrorLine> with no window/ack context; IssuesPage defaults to window=7d active-only (IssuesPage.tsx:26,64) and a zero-match q filter falls through to IssuesPanel's EmptyState 'No issues recorded.' (IssuesPanel.tsx:229-249) with only a small q chip above it. The audit page freely shows rows older than 7d (offset pagination over 1.2M rows), so pivoting from any such error row asserts an all-clear the system cannot back — the group exists, just outside the default window or acknowledged.
findings.detail: Fix: carry window=all on the pivot link, and make the zero-rows-with-active-filters state name the narrowing ('no match for "…" in the last 7 days — widen to All time / check acknowledged') instead of rendering the unqualified all-clear copy.

findings.title: Keyboard triage stops one verb short of the hot loop — selected row cannot expand occurrences or open its View link
findings.evidence: IssuesPage registers only j/k + 'a' (IssuesPage.tsx:195-220); useListTriage supports arbitrary verbs (use-list-triage.ts:42-68) but no o/Enter verb expands the selected row's occurrences or follows issue.link. The triage loop is select → inspect evidence → ack; the middle (evidence) step is mouse-only — DisclosureRow is tab-reachable but tabbing abandons the j/k cursor. AuditLogPage has no list-triage at all (no useListTriage import): row expansion there is DisclosureRow-tab-walk only, with no j/k over 20-row pages.
findings.detail: Shared-primitive-frozen-at-beachhead pattern: useListTriage shipped to Issues with the minimum verb set and never reached the audit table. Add o=expand / Enter=View verbs on Issues; adopt useListTriage on /audit-log rows.

findings.title: Audit detail's Request ID is still plain text while the /sessions?request= door now exists two components away (strengthens known-deferred request_id dead-end)
findings.evidence:
AuditLogTable.tsx:328-335 renders entry.request_id as a bare

; the pivot mechanism is live and consumed: SessionsPage hydrates ?request= into its filter (SessionsPage.tsx:86) and IssuesPanel's occurrences rows already link `/sessions?request=…` (IssuesPanel.tsx:147-154). The dead-end is now an intra-surface inconsistency — the same audit row linked from an issue group gets a Session→ door, but the same row opened on /audit-log does not.
findings.detail: NEW strengthening evidence for the known-deferred item, not a rediscovery: the cost dropped to a one-line Link and the inconsistency is now visible within the issues↔audit pair itself. Note most audit rows have NULL request_id (llm_api_call rows live-sampled), so the door renders only where the spine actually exists — honest by construction.

findings.title: 'From' date filter is interpreted as UTC midnight, not owner-timezone midnight
findings.evidence: AuditLogPage's since input is type=date (AuditLogPage.tsx:248-254) sent as YYYY-MM-DD; FastAPI parses it to a naive datetime (audit.py:308) compared against timestamptz ts, i.e. UTC midnight. The fleet just completed an owner-timezone day-key sweep (bu-jlzxf et al., frontend/src/lib/day-window helper) that did not cover this filter — for a UTC+8 owner, 'From 2026-07-10' includes the last 8 hours of their 07-09.
findings.detail: New instance of the owner-tz class on a surface the sweep missed; route through the same lib/day-window convention the swept endpoints use.

audits.jarvis_gap: The 07-10 program's mechanisms verifiably shipped and are wired end-to-end: sources_degraded flows from DegradedSources through meta into a named SourceDegradedNote that suppresses the all-clear (issues.py:336-391 → IssuesPage.tsx:85 → IssuesPanel.tsx:220-249); windows/severity/butler pills are URL-truth; j/k+a triage with an honest footer hint strip; outcome column, actor/action pivots, acknowledge-until-recurrence with real watermarks. What separates this from JARVIS-grade is that the trace spine breaks under live load exactly where it matters most: the top issue group in today's feed cannot be drilled (poisoned-metadata 400), the second-most-visible group 404s on expansion (window-dependent key drift), two distinct groups share one issue_key so an ack silently swallows both, and the audit page — the root-evidence ledger — 500s outright on filters as ordinary as actor=memory, while telling the owner to 'try again shortly'. The doors are built; several open onto broken stairs, and the surface still asserts calm ('No issues recorded.', 'temporarily unavailable') in states where the system cannot prove either claim.
audits.ideal: Opening /issues answers 'what is broken and is it being handled' in five seconds: a windowed, severity-first feed where every group has one stable, window-independent identity (hash of the normalized error, never a truncated slug), an ack that provably holds across every view until real recurrence, and a drilldown that always opens — Seen Nx expands to exactly those N rows for the window in view ('showing 50 of N', load-more), each row a door: Session → the spawn transcript, request_id → the request trace, actor → the butler. The audit ledger beneath it never dies on a row — deserialization is total over whatever history contains, and a repair migration has already normalized the 3-week poisoned band. Every active predicate on /audit-log is a visible, dismissable chip (result, noise class, key, actor, since-in-owner-tz), so the ledger can never be silently narrower than it claims; pivots between the two pages carry their full context (window, noise, ack state) so a hop never lands on a false all-clear. The whole loop — next issue, inspect evidence, acknowledge, verify in ledger — runs from the keyboard: j/k to select, o to open evidence, Enter to follow the door, a to ack, on both pages via the same shared triage primitive.

moves.title: Repair the poisoned audit-metadata band and make deserialization total
moves.why: 349,113 rows (29% of public.audit_log, 2026-06-14→07-05) hold string-typed metadata that 500s any page containing one — the audit surface's worst live failure, and it impersonates a transient outage.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Tolerant AuditLogEntry.from_record: json.loads fallback for str metadata + unit test with a poisoned fixture row (unblocks everything immediately). 2) One-shot repair migration: UPDATE ... SET metadata = metadata #>> '{}'::jsonb-parsed WHERE jsonb_typeof(metadata)='string', batched, with count parity check. 3) Contract test asserting GET /api/audit-log never 500s over a table seeded with all three metadata typeofs.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/api/models/audit.py:from_record; new core alembic migration (serialize revision number — parallel-migration collision hazard); tests/ audit contract suite; owner doctrine prefers the cleanup migration over a permanent compat shim, but the shim is the safety net.

findings.title: Stale export can render with real-data authority: 14-day trust window, no as-of anywhere, and a single-file bind-mount inode risk
findings.detail: compute_decision_digest trusts the export until it is 14 days old (_STALE_EXPORT_AGE, decision_review.py:131) yet the UI renders ages to the hour ('waiting 3h') computed against now — a 13-day-stale export shows closed decisions as open and misses new ones with zero visual tell. The API meta carries only decisions_available/unavailable_reason (decisions.py:50-57), never the export mtime, so no frontend could render an 'as of' plaque even if it wanted to. Compounding: docker-compose.yml:602,733 bind-mounts the single FILE .beads/issues.export.jsonl:ro; if bd's auto-export replaces it by atomic rename (temp+rename), the container keeps the original inode and silently serves a frozen snapshot from container start until day 14 flips it to export_stale (inferred — needs an inode check across one bd write once the post-merge stack is up). Also the verdict opener hardcodes the reason 'beads export unreachable' (decisions-verdict-opener.tsx:39) instead of passing through meta.unavailable_reason, which distinguishes export_missing/export_stale/read_error — the page-level SourceDegradedNote does use it (DecisionsPage.tsx:186).

audits.ideal: The ideal Decision Desk is one surface where every open owner decision — detected from structured fields, never a title regex — appears within minutes of creation, reads completely in place (the question, the options with the owner-silent default marked, the deadline as a countdown chip, what it blocks and for how long, and the full description prose), and closes in one keystroke: j/k to the row, number keys or Enter to pick an option, with the choice written back to the bead, the attention ledger, and decision memory so the system never re-asks. The verdict line ('2 decisions waiting, oldest 5d, 1 blocking a deploy') is computed from the same digest that drives Telegram escalation — one fact, one number — and carries an as-of plaque naming the export's true age; a stale or unreachable export renders as a loud named degradation within hours, not after 14 silent days. Approvals and Decisions read as the two lanes of a single trust instrument: same triage grammar (j/k/a-d-x vs j/k/1-2-3), same undo-window contract, same door density — every id a link, every escalation clause a jump to the blocked artifact.

findings.title: Conflict radar scans un-collapsed duplicate rows: 12 phantom overlap warnings for a week containing one real lunch
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/calendar/workspace/conflicts (2026-07-12..19) returns 14 issues (12 overlap + 2 overloaded_day) referencing 8 distinct entry_ids, while GET /api/calendar/workspace for the same window returns only 4 visible entries — the workspace read collapses the 3-member origin_ref duplicate cluster (GET /duplicates: member_count=3, match_pass=origin_ref) that the radar pairs combinatorially. Code: query_calendar_conflicts (src/butlers/api/read_models/calendar_workspace_v1.py:974-1050) feeds query_calendar_workspace rows straight into detect_conflict_issues with no _dedup_workspace_rows pass; the duplicates endpoint docstring (src/butlers/api/routers/calendar_workspace.py:1638-1645) confirms the main read 'silently collapses' those same rows.
findings.detail: Three systemic sins at once: (1) one fact, many numbers — the radar computes from a different row set than the grid it annotates; (2) fabricated urgency — 'overloaded_day' warnings are summed from duplicate hours of a single event, and the banner one-liner would read '12 overlaps · a packed day' over a visibly quiet week, destroying earned calm and training the owner to dismiss the radar; (3) drill-down dead end — expanded issue cards list event titles whose entry_ids (8f045890, ae81f360, 73f7b00c, 8d18f3a1) do not exist on the rendered grid, and the amber overlap-edge set (CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2494-2502) references those invisible ids.

findings.title: Live calendar projection has had no provider sync since 2026-04-07 (96+ days); grid renders an authoritative-looking week with zero grid-level staleness signal
findings.evidence: Live: every one of the 10 source_freshness rows reports sync_state=stale with last_synced_at/last_success_at of 2026-03-30..2026-04-07 or null, last_error empty (staleness_ms ~8.9e9 ≈ 103 days); GET /api/calendar/accounts reports both Google accounts health.state='unknown', last_heartbeat_at=null, health_available=false. Yet the week grid renders events at full authority. Backend has a sync poller (src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:_run sync poller ~8060 and _upsert_projection_cursor:6859) that should stamp calendar_sync_cursors on every run — nothing has stamped since April, with no recorded error.
findings.detail: Dual finding. (a) Ops: the provider sync loop is silently dead on the live stack — no failure row, no escalation, no QA discovery; a calendar whose ingest died in April still presents as a working calendar (failure impersonating health at the system level). (b) Design: this is NEW strengthening evidence for the consciously-deferred 'freshness plaque' — the staleness truth exists only as small degraded dots inside the Sources tab; the grid, masthead, and day/week views give the owner no clue their week is a 3-month-old snapshot. Five-second verification fails completely: the owner cannot distinguish 'my week' from 'my week as of March 30'.

findings.title: Test artifact 'provider:google:__invalid_check__' persisted into the live freshness ledger and renders as a real Google source
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/calendar/workspace source_freshness includes {source_key: 'provider:google:__invalid_check__', sync_state: 'stale', last_synced_at: null}. The only writers of that calendar_id are tests (tests/modules/test_module_calendar.py:385,529,557 — invalid-calendar error-path probes). Frontend sourceName()/titleize() (CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:249-285) will render it in the Sources rail as '[Google] Invalid Check ' with a permanent degraded dot and a working show/hide toggle (lines 5933-6023).
findings.detail: Test pollution wearing real-data authority (systemic sin #1): a canary probe against the live stack minted a permanent source row that the UI presents as a genuine, permanently-degraded calendar. There is no prune/archive path for calendar sources (the bu-33dm2 soft-archive covers ingestion endpoint identities, not calendar_sources). It also permanently drags on the honest-freshness signal — one source can never be anything but stale.

findings.title: Same-origin_ref duplicate with an 8h-drifted window escapes the origin_ref dedup pass — 'Lou Shang — Last Day' renders twice, one copy with a wrong window
findings.evidence: Live: workspace returns two entries for origin_ref qvj8349mbs1i5imh2370bdd508, same source_key provider:google:uniquosity@gmail.com, same butler (lifestyle): 3aa6ea5f (2026-07-13T16:00Z→14T16:00Z = midnight-SGT-aligned all-day) and 4a3ad1d7 (2026-07-14T00:00Z→15T00:00Z = UTC-midnight-aligned), both all_day=false. GET /duplicates does NOT cluster them: the cluster_key embeds the start-ms ('origin_ref\x01<ref>\x011783828800000' in the lunch cluster), so time-drifted copies of one provider event form two singleton clusters and the dedup pass never sees them.
findings.detail: The owner sees the same farewell event on two day slabs, one spanning 08:00→08:00 the next day (a timezone misread of an all-day event), and the radar then converts the pair into overlap + overloaded_day warnings. Because incremental sync is dead (finding 2), the stale-windowed row is never superseded. The origin_ref match pass should key on origin_ref alone (keep newest row) — a provider event id is already a unique identity; including start-ms makes the strongest dedup pass blind to exactly the corruption it exists to catch.

findings.title: Degraded conflict scan is consumed as total silence — indistinguishable from a clean week, contrary to the fleet's 'never suppress' convention
findings.evidence: ConflictRadarBanner.tsx:164 'if (!available || issues.length === 0 || dismissed) return null' with the header comment (lines 11-14) declaring silence the intended degraded mode; CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2487-2492 additionally maps conflictsQuery HTTP errors into conflictScan=undefined → issues_available ?? false → the same silence (isError never read); the amber overlap edges also vanish (2496). CLAUDE.md fleet convention: 'name the degraded source inline with an em-dash, never suppress it.'
findings.detail: Grading of the landed bu-jad4j 'calendar conflicts.available' item: the flag IS consumed (registered in src/api/types.degraded-flags.test.ts:85), but the chosen consumption is suppression — a degraded scan and a genuinely clear week produce identical pixels, and the loss of amber overlap edges silently downgrades the grid's warning layer. One SourceDegradedNote line above the grid ('Conflict radar — scan unavailable') is the convention-conformant shape. Note: fixing finding 1 is a prerequisite for this note to be worth reading.

audits.jarvis_gap: The built surface is close to the bar — Dispatch-language chrome, drag/resize with recurrence scopes, durable undo with session doors, honest soft-failure mutation gates, degraded flags consumed on audit/people/accounts. The gap is that the instruments are now more trustworthy than the data feeding them: on the live stack the provider sync has been silently dead since April 7 with no error, no escalation, and no grid-level staleness signal, so the owner is shown a confident 3-month-old snapshot of their week; and the conflict radar — the surface's flagship proactive instrument — computes from un-collapsed duplicate rows the grid itself hides, emitting 12 phantom overlap warnings plus fabricated 'packed day' verdicts for a week with one real lunch. A JARVIS whose calendar warns loudly about ghosts while not noticing its own ingest died in spring fails both 'earned calm' and 'failure never impersonates health' — not in the pixels, which are honest per-flag, but in the spine those flags stand on.

The conflict radar runs on exactly the rows the grid renders — dedup-collapsed, keep-separate honored, butler-projected copies of the owner's own events excluded from pairing — so every warning it raises corresponds to something the owner can see and act on in one hop, and a degraded scan says so in one named line rather than silence. Sync death is impossible to miss: a poller that hasn't stamped a cursor within 2× its interval self-reports into QA discovery and the attention ledger. The whole loop is keyboard-first: [ ] page periods, m/w/d/l switch views, c creates, t recenters, Enter opens the focused entry's detail with its fresh server copy, session door, linked people, and one-keystroke undo.

audits.ideal: The ideal /spend opens with a verdict that always has a real referent: "On pace — $3.99/day against a $150 ceiling, 29% used, normal confidence" or "Projected to breach the ceiling by $23 on Jul 26 — top driver travel/upcoming-travel-check" or "No ceiling set — $3.99/day unpaced; set one" — one line, every clause a door, never contradicted by an adjacent alert. The enforced number and the displayed number are the same ledger row (bu-7o89u), and every panel below it answers one question on one shared window: the TimeWindowPicker scopes daily chart, movers, top sessions, by-schedule AND breakdown identically, with any dimension that must use a different source naming its basis inline. The evidence layer reads the same DB pools the posture layer does, so 'Most Expensive Sessions' can never silently omit the fleet's biggest spenders because a sidecar socket flaked — MCP is the fallback, not the plane. Every fan-out and every singleton read (rules, ceiling) either succeeds or names itself degraded; a 200-with-empty is provably a true empty. findings.title: Memory list/detail/activity/inspect endpoints silently drop failing pools — degraded honesty shipped for /stats only
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py: _fan_out_memory_queries accepts a DegradedSources tracker (lines 106-158) but only get_stats passes one (line 275-281, 308). list_episodes (382-387), list_facts (518-522), list_rules (769-773), list_activity (~953), inspect, and the by-id fan-outs all call it with no tracker, so a genuinely unreachable pool is indistinguishable from a truthful empty/complete result. findings.title: Detail trio fabricates 'not in the ledger' on any error — isError dropped and pool outage becomes 404, two layers deep

(lines 218-225). The Page shell HAS an error prop with retry (frontend/src/components/ui/page.tsx:44-48, priority loading > error > empty) that none of the three pages pass. Backend doubles the fabrication: get_fact/get_rule/get_episode fan out with no tracker and raise 404 "not found" when results are empty (memory.py:576-577, 429-430) — a downed pool that OWNS the record yields the same 404 as true absence, so a chronicler-owned record (chronicler pool is failing live today) would render as "not in the ledger" when it is in the ledger. bu-mkd5r (#3031) completed the three-way contract on every /memory band but did not touch the detail pages (git log confirms); bu-tpudw.2's 404-vs-503 fix covered sessions only. New instance of sin 2 + sin 7.

findings.title: Re-embed action scope ≠ drift measurement scope: fleet-wide stale count, single-pool action the owner can never reconcile

But POST /api/memory/reembed runs on exactly ONE butler pool (memory.py:2380-2400) and HousekeepingBand hardcodes the alphabetically-first butler (HousekeepingBand.tsx:373-377, 414, 441). The owner sees "4,631 rows on an old embedding", arms and commits re-embed, gets "re-embedded N rows" for one pool, and the pending refetch still shows thousands — the surface's one commit action cannot clear the number it advertises. The in-code comment (HousekeepingBand.tsx:368-371) claiming the pending count "probes the first available pool ... targets the same pool the counts were measured on" is factually wrong per the backend. Sin 8 (one fact, many numbers/scopes).

findings.title: Attention rail conditions 4-5 sources unguarded: an errored fading-count or reembed-pending fetch silently renders 'Nothing waiting.'

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/relationship/CirclesPage.tsx:61 (FETCH_LIMIT = 500) + :401 (useGroups({ offset: 0, limit: FETCH_LIMIT })) vs roster/relationship/api/router.py:555 (limit: int = Query(50, ge=1, le=200)). The bu-tpudw.5 contract-test registry pattern (degraded envelopes) is the natural home for a 'FE request params satisfy backend Query constraints' check.

audits.jarvis_gap: Plex/Index/Detail are near the bar — scoped keyboard maps, honest per-source degraded notes (bu-hckjv verified live in GiftsPanel/LoansPanel/MessageThreads/LinkedContact/workbench facts), provenance doors, drag-to-retier with undo-equivalent unpin — but the surface still tells two attention truths (the rail's client-side urgency contradicts the butler's compute_urgency engine on every tier and ignores stay-in-touch overrides), one of five routes (/entities/circles) 422s on every load behind fully-mocked tests, and drill-down context (Concentration→Detail origin, Index filter scope for j/k) is discarded mid-hop, so clauses stop one hop short of the trace the owner actually walked.

Every mark, halo satellite, and capacity meter is provable one hop deep and every fetch failure is named per-source (including the halo). Index is the curation workbench: filter chips in the URL, full keyboard map, bulk actions that keep failures selected — and detail inherits that exact scope so j/k walks the list the owner filtered. Detail is a single-headline dossier where every clause is a door (fact → provenance grid, thread → session, tier → cadence math), archive is undoable, and breadcrumbs reproduce the real navigation path via origin params set by every producing lens. Circles and Concentration are lenses over the same graph that always load, state their truncation arithmetic honestly, and contain zero client functions pointed at routes the backend no longer serves — enforced by a contract gate that validates every api/client.ts path and query constraint against the live OpenAPI schema.

findings.title: Model catalog presents 23-day-stale verification as current health, with no error evidence and an invisible routing consequence
findings.evidence: Live GET /api/settings/models: all 31 entries carry last_verified_at=2026-06-19 (23 days before today, 2026-07-12); discretion-qwen3.5-9b has last_verified_ok=false with NO error-message field (the reason exists only in a server log — model_settings.py:687 logger.warning; the UPDATE at :697-699 persists only at/latency/ok). FE ModelRow (SettingsModelsPage.tsx:1378-1411) renders a bare ✓/✗ glyph with no timestamp, no age, no error text, and no statement of consequence — yet model_routing.py:295/:370/:485 excludes last_verified_ok=false entries from fleet routing, so the ✗ is an enforcement fact, not a passive status. verify-all exists only as a manual POST (model_settings.py:617, rate-limited); grep confirms no cron/background caller. The /settings console KPI 'Models OK 11/18' (fetchModelStats, SettingsConsolePage.tsx:94-103) and the standing red attention item 'Model verification failed: discretion-qwen3.5-9b' are both computed from this month-old probe and presented with real-data authority.
findings.detail: Sins #1 (stale data with current-data authority) + #3 (✗ → dead end, evidence is log-only) + #9 (verification lifecycle stalls after one manual run). The owner cannot answer 'is this model actually broken right now, and why?' from any pixel; the only recovery is knowing to press Verify all. Not covered by bu-a63hn (that staleness loop is for the secrets credential store, per DirectionPassport.tsx comment) nor any 07-10 epic/deferred item.

findings.title: Permissions 'Audit reel' privileged preset is drowned by routine LLM traffic while its UI copy promises the opposite
findings.evidence: Live GET /api/audit-log?limit=15&kind=privileged returns ['llm_api_call','session' ×5 pairs, ...] — 10 of 15 rows are per-LLM-call bookkeeping from switchboard. Backend filter (src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py:404-406) excludes only action NOT LIKE '%_heartbeat' and NOT LIKE 'GET /%'. The page section (SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:1307) claims: 'Last 15 privileged-action entries: permission changes, data operations, and webhook events. Heartbeat and routine traffic excluded.' On a busy fleet an actual permission flip is pushed out of the 15-row window within seconds.
findings.detail: Inverse fabrication: noise impersonating signal on the accountability surface — the owner cannot see their last permission change (five-second-verification failure). Adjacent to the deferred /audit-log 'principal/subsystem split' deep move, but this is new concrete evidence that the shipped kind=privileged contract fails its own displayed promise; fix is a filter-level exclusion/allowlist, not the full audit-page rebuild.
