findings.title: Settings console computes each headline fact twice from different endpoints, and ConsoleClock leaks its interval
findings.evidence: One screen, two sources per fact: KPI strip reads header_counts from GET /settings/console (models_verified/total, open_approvals, spend) while the panels independently recompute the same numbers from GET /settings/models (fetchModelStats, SettingsConsolePage.tsx:94-103), GET /approvals/metrics (:105-109), and GET /spend?period=30d (:90-92) — consistent live today (11/18, 36) but structurally free to disagree within one viewport. Separately, ConsoleClock (:186-199) returns its clearInterval cleanup from inside the setTimeout callback where it is discarded — the 60s interval is never cleared, leaking one interval + post-unmount setState per /settings visit.
findings.detail: Sin #8 shape (one fact, many numbers) in its mildest form, plus a small correctness leak. Excludes the spend rolling-30d-labeled-MTD mislabel, which is in-flight (bu-7o89u.2). Fix: panels render from the single console envelope (or the envelope carries per-panel detail), and the clock keeps the interval id in a ref cleared by the effect cleanup.

audits.ideal: The JARVIS-grade settings-secrets quadrant is the household's controls-and-keys room, where every status pixel is a proof: the console opens with an attention strip whose every red item is a working door that lands focused on the exact failing object (?focus=c:cli-auth/claude, not a dead ?tab=), and a KPI strip whose numbers are single-sourced from one envelope so the same fact can never disagree with itself one panel down. The model catalog is a live truth surface — a background verify loop keeps every entry's probe younger than a stated SLA, each ✓/✗ carries its age ('verified 4h ago' / amber '23d stale'), a ✗ states its enforcement consequence ('excluded from routing since Jun 19') and opens onto the stored error text and the verify attempt that produced it. Permissions is the accountability ledger: the audit reel actually contains only privileged actions (permission flips, exports, webhook mutations) with each row's required reason readable inline by keyboard and screen reader, fetch failures render as named degraded notes with retry — never as 'No recent audit entries' — and every destructive control (webhook delete included) is confirmed or undoable. Secrets keeps its passport metaphor with the already-honest degraded banners, gains the credential-health feed and keyboard triage already queued, and the whole quadrant shares one query boundary, one Tip primitive, and zero raw-fetch bypasses.
audits.jarvis_gap: Five-second verification holds at the console's front door (attention strip is honest, KPI nulls render as em-dashes) but the trace spine breaks exactly at the last hop on 2 of the 3 live red items: auth_renewal deep-links to a dead ?tab= param, and model_error lands on a catalog where the failure has no timestamp, no error text, and no visible consequence — while the underlying probe data is 23 days stale and silently governs fleet routing. The accountability loop is likewise unproven: the 'privileged' audit reel is 2/3 routine LLM-call noise, permission reasons live only in mouse-hover tooltips, and permissions-page fetch errors impersonate calm empty states. Earned calm is real on /secrets and the console header; it is not yet earned on the model catalog or the permissions ledger.

findings.title: Stalled curriculum build impersonates live progress — owner's ONLY curriculum has been 'being built' for 21 days
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/education/mind-maps/d3758b20-... returns nodes:0, edges:0, root_node_id:null, created_at==updated_at==2026-06-21 (21 days ago); GET /api/education/quiz-responses for it returns 0 rows. UI: frontend/src/components/education/MindMapGraph.tsx:161 renders "This curriculum has no concepts yet. The butler is still building it." for any empty map, unconditionally. Backend: roster/education/api/router.py `_trigger_curriculum_drain` fires a fire-and-forget ephemeral session (asyncio.create_task, returns 202); if that session dies after creating the map row, nothing records the failure and no surface reads it — no build ledger, no session door, no staleness clamp, no retry affordance.
findings.detail: Sins 1+3+9 in one place: fabricated activity claim with real-data authority ('the butler is still building it' — the system cannot prove any butler is doing anything), drill-down dead end (zero doors from the stalled map to the session that was supposed to build it), and a lifecycle stalled at the last step with no alarm. This is the exact class the QA breaker-truth epic (bu-533qx) just purged elsewhere. The whole surface is currently a shrine to one dead request.

Keep learning and reviews will appear here." whenever allEntries is empty, including while queries are in flight or after every query failed.

audits.jarvis_gap: The page cannot answer the JARVIS question 'is my learning system alive and what needs me now?' — it opens on a graph of a curriculum that died mid-build 21 days ago while claiming the butler is still working, buries the actionable signal (overdue reviews) behind a tab whose fan-out silently drops failures, offers zero doors from any claim to its evidence (no session link for the build, no quiz-session trace), and speaks a pre-Dispatch visual dialect with four disagreeing status→color maps. Five-second verification, earned calm, and the unbroken trace spine all fail here; only the request-curriculum verb and page-level error honesty meet the bar.

audits.ideal: Education opens as a Dispatch-dialect learning desk that verifies itself in five seconds: a header verdict line (N overdue reviews · last quiz 2d ago · 1 curriculum building — door to the live session), the review queue first (overdue at top, j/k + Enter into node detail, per-map degraded notes when any curriculum's reviews are unreachable), and the concept map as the second lens with one shared mastery-progression token scale across graph, panel, chips, and buckets. Every rendered claim is provable: a curriculum shows 'building' only while a live session door exists, flips to an honest 'build failed 3w ago — Retry' when the trace goes cold, and each mastery number doors through to the quiz responses and the session that produced them. All dates in owner tz via <Time>, all colors from index.css tokens, empty states that teach ('Request curriculum' as both button and palette verb), and no query error anywhere renders as calm.

findings.title: Archive spine corrupted by a 1904 calendar-birthday episode: earliest_date is unclamped MIN(start_at), so /chronicles claims 122 years of navigable history and renders a fabricated 17-hour day in 1904
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/chronicler/briefing?date=2026-07-11 returns "earliest_date":"1904-10-18"; GET /api/chronicler/episodes?overlaps_start=1904-10-17... returns episode 72b371a6 source_name=google_calendar.completed, title "Hui Min Lee's birthday", start 1904-10-18T00:00Z end 1904-10-19 (birth-year recurring event ingested at its literal origin date, created_at 2026-05-03). GET /briefing?date=1904-10-18 renders recent_days [{date:1904-10-18, total_minutes:1024, episode_count:1}] — a 17h04m 'recorded' day fabricated from a pure intent-layer block. Producer: src/butlers/chronicler/editorial.py:530-534 `SELECT MIN(start_at) FROM episodes WHERE tombstone_at IS NULL` with no sanity floor; frontend/src/pages/ChroniclesPage.tsx:161-162 uses it as the backward clamp, so `[` steps through ~44,000 empty days.
findings.detail: Two defects compound: (1) ingestion projects all-day recurring birthday/anniversary events at their origin year instead of the occurrence year (or dropping them); (2) the archive bound trusts raw MIN with no plausibility clamp, so one corrupt row silently extends the owner's 'lived history' by 122 years with real-data authority. Fails 'nothing fabricated' — the 1904 recent-days row presents intent minutes as recorded time on a day the owner was not alive.

findings.title: ManualRefreshButton is frozen at the pre-IEA query families: it invalidates the retired pie's dead byDay/byCategory keys and none of the seven live IEA queries, while the panel has polling disabled — so Refresh is the only refresh path and it refreshes almost nothing visible

ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:89 sets `refetchInterval = false` for the whole panel.

[]` to DayRibbon without isError → DayRibbon.tsx:113-123 renders 'No activity recorded for this window.' on failure. StreakCallouts.tsx:63 `if (isError) return null` — streaks silently vanish. audits.jarvis_gap: The IEA reframe genuinely landed: the page opens with an honest editorial voice over a settled day, the ribbon/balance/trends/who panels are wired to real endpoints with three-state honesty, and evidence chains are one click away. What still separates it from JARVIS: the archive spine can be poisoned by one corrupt row (1904 bound) so the system asserts history it cannot prove; the one manual refresh affordance silently no-ops on the panels the owner is looking at; the older seam components (ribbon episodes, map trail, badge strip) still let failure impersonate an empty day; and the archive is walkable only one day at a time — no jump-to-date, no click-through from a trend anomaly to its day — so 'what happened that Tuesday?' costs dozens of keystrokes instead of one.
audits.ideal: The ideal /chronicles is a provable autobiography: it opens on the last settled day with a voice paragraph derived only from corroborated activity, and every number on screen reconciles to one counting rule (activity-layer union) or is explicitly labeled otherwise. The archive bound is the first day the chronicler actually observed, clamped against corrupt timestamps, and any day is one gesture away — 'g' opens a go-to-date field, recent-days paginates deeper, and every trend bar, streak badge, and anomaly flag is a door that lands on its day with the relevant panel focused. Failure is always louder than absence: a dead episodes query says so in the ribbon, a dead source-state fetch degrades the badge strip rather than deleting it, and Refresh provably refetches everything visible for the window or says what it could not. Every block on the ribbon and every bar on the Gantt is keyboard-operable into the same EpisodeDrawer evidence chain, so 'why is this counted?' is answerable without a mouse in under five seconds.

findings.title: Failed investigations impersonate in-flight 'detect' cases across the entire surface (no 'failed' state exists)
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/qa/severity.py:44-60 — state_of_case maps terminal statuses failed/timeout/anonymization_failed (without human-action markers) to the fallback "detect"; CaseState Literal (severity.py:13) and StateTrack.tsx:3,10-15 have no failed terminus. (PRPanel.tsx:38 — implying one is coming), and CaseDossierHeader.tsx:10,54-56 withholds the retry button (TERMINAL_STAGES=[landed,escalated]) while offering dismiss — even though the backend treats failed as terminal and retryable (core/healing/tracking.py:91-93 TERMINAL_STATUSES includes failed; healing.py:488 retry gate accepts it). Downstream contradiction: KPI "active cases · now = 0" (qa.py SQL counts dispatch_pending/investigating/pr_open) sits directly above a rail listing the same two cases as apparently-live detect items — one fact, two numbers.
findings.detail: Root cause is one fallthrough line; symptoms fan out: dead cases look active, the wanted affordance (retry) is denied exactly where it applies, the dossier reads as an in-flight case, and the KPI contradicts the rail. Sins (1) failure impersonating progress and (8) one-fact-many-numbers.

findings.title: Verdict is structurally blind to staffer death and failing streaks — the watcher has no watcher on its own surface
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/qa.py:1544-1552 — staffer_status='healthy' unless breaker tripped, no history, or last patrol status=='error'; no staleness term comparing last_patrol_at to patrol_interval_minutes (both already on the same wire response). qa.py summary construction hardcodes next_patrol_at=None ('Requires scheduler integration'), so QaVerdictOpener.tsx:57's 'next patrol …' all-clear clause is permanently dead code. Pre-trip streaks are invisible: live circuit_breaker.consecutive_failures=2 renders as plain 'Circuit breaker closed' (QaOverviewPage.tsx:300) and verdict all-clear — at 4/5 the page would still be fully calm. Live corroboration of the blind spot's cost: the staffer's runtime CLI auth is dead (journal: 'refresh token was revoked'), every investigation fails in seconds, yet /api/qa/summary says staffer_status='healthy'; credentials_status covers only gh_token/git author (qa.py:1553-1590), not runtime CLI auth. Note bu-9r3hd.4's InfraStateSource + external deadman run INSIDE the staffer's own patrol pipeline (commit f5f6fbb4f), so staffer-process death silences those checks too — /qa would read 'QA staffer healthy: last patrol 3d ago' indefinitely.
findings.detail: Fails five-second fleet verification at the root: the one surface whose job is watching the fleet cannot see its own death or its own credential rot. The fix is cheap — the FE already receives last_patrol_at + patrol_interval_minutes and consecutive_failures; nobody computes 'overdue' or names the streak.

audits.jarvis_gap: The three ingestion routes are among the most mature Dispatch surfaces: the timeline ledger has honest hour totals from the histogram, a real error state with retry, trace/minute scope banners, URL-backed drawer, saved views with divergence dots, and the live badge distinguishes Down from Idle; the roster consumes both hourly and device-liveness degraded flags. What separates it from JARVIS-grade is lifecycle closure and forked truth: the connector-attention concept exists twice (roster vs timeline) with different data sources, different predicates, and different affordances — the timeline fork still resurrects identities the owner deliberately archived and offers no door to their evidence; the archive lifecycle is one-way in pixels (archive is one click, unarchive exists only as an unused endpoint); and a whole tier of backend-complete, freshly audit-hardened lifecycle controls (pause/run-now/disconnect/rotate-token) has zero reachable pixels, with dead props waiting in the detail view. The diagnostic drill-down page still lets failed sub-queries impersonate 'No incidents recorded.'
audits.movement_claim: improved — bu-lkzsf failed-status is live-confirmed end-to-end (GET /api/ingestion/events?statuses=failed returns real rows; chips, hour-group error totals, and drawer treatment all consume it) and bu-33dm2/bu-u19yv soft-archive is live-confirmed on the roster (2 archived identities split out, review queue wired to the audit-logged endpoint); the new findings are beachhead escapes, not regressions

findings.title: Timeline attention strip is a stale fork that resurrects archived connectors and dead-ends drill-down
findings.evidence: TimelineTab.tsx:787-819 (ConnectorAttentionStrip) is a second, divergent implementation of the roster's connectors/AttentionStrip.tsx:41. It reads useConnectorSummaries → GET /api/switchboard/connectors, whose payload has NO `archived` field (live-confirmed: 27 rows vs 25 from /api/ingestion/connectors/summaries), and filters on raw `state !== 'healthy' || liveness === 'offline'` instead of deriveConnectorDispatchInfo. Live: both soft-archived identities (google_health:degraded, google_health:...uniquosity...:activity) satisfy the predicate and render as permanent "Connector issues:" on /ingestion — the exact fleet-health drag bu-33dm2 archived them to remove. Strip items are underlined <span>s with title= tooltips, not Links (roster strip items link to connector detail): underline promises a door that does not exist, and the error_message hides in a hover title (the pattern bu-sywxz swept elsewhere).
findings.detail: Sin #7 (shared gate ships with a sibling surface exempted) + sin #3 (drill-down dead end) + two verdict vocabularies for one fact (10 attention rows via timeline predicate vs 8 via roster predicate, live). Fix is deletion, not addition: retire the bespoke strip and mount the roster's AttentionStrip fed by the archived-aware summaries endpoint.

findings.title: Archive lifecycle is one-way in the UI: one-click archive with no undo, unarchive endpoint has zero pixel readers
findings.evidence: ArchiveCandidatesList.tsx:123-136 fires useArchiveConnector on a single un-confirmed click; on success the identity immediately leaves the active roster and fleet rollups. Backend POST .../unarchive exists and its own docstring calls archiving "a soft, reversible state" (ingestion_connectors.py:948-975), but `grep -rn unarchive frontend/src` shows wiring only for contacts and memory entities — none for connectors. ArchivedConnectorsList.tsx:103-105 offers only "history →"; no restore affordance anywhere.
findings.detail: Design-bar Recovery bias: prefer undo over confirm only when the undo actually exists — here neither exists. Calendar just shipped the durable-Undo pattern (bu-4cmc1); this surface shipped the destructive half only. Mis-click cost: identity silently vanishes from KPIs/attention with no in-UI path back (owner must curl the endpoint). Matches the redesign-reconciliation wiring-audit failure mode.

findings.title: Connector lifecycle controls are backend-complete but unreachable: pause/run-now render as dead props, disconnect/rotate-token have no surface at all

ConnectorDetailView.tsx:126-129 declares onPause/onRunNow and renders 'pause poll'/'run now' buttons at :372-393 — but ConnectorDetailPage.tsx:246-255 passes only onReauth/onSetPrimaryAccount, and a repo-wide grep finds no caller passing onPause/onRunNow. No FE client function exists for pause/run-now/disconnect/rotate-token (client.ts has only archiveConnector).
findings.detail: Sin #6 (capability shipped backend-only with zero pixel readers) — worse, the pixels were half-built and left disconnected, so the component advertises an affordance the page can never light up. Either wire the pair on the detail page (with a visible paused state and run-now feedback) plus a deliberate home for disconnect/rotate-token, or delete the dead props; the current state is cruft posing as capability.

findings.title: Connector detail sub-queries render errors as calm empties: 'No incidents recorded.' from a dead incidents source

The page's own primary query handles error via the Page shell, so the pattern was known and stopped one layer short.

[]` (:144) with no error path. A failed GET /switchboard/ingestion-rules therefore shows a confident, wrong description of the whole filtering policy while one sub-block quietly errors.

findings.title: Roster attention strip labels an offline connector 'authorized' in green — the reason for attention is never stated

For offline connectors deriveConnectorDispatchInfo returns authStatus 'ok' (connector-auth.ts:81-88), so the strip currently shows six offline google_health identities (live) tagged with a green 'authorized' — the one word shown is the one axis that is fine, while the actual reason ('connector offline · check connectivity', available in info.authNote, and healthVerdictWord) is unused.
findings.detail: Information-design defect: a 'needs attention' list whose per-item label can be a green all-clear word forces click-through to learn why. Render healthVerdictWord (offline/degraded/error) as the tag, with authStatusLabel only when auth is the reason.

audits.ideal: The ideal ingestion surface is one instrument with one truth per fact: a single connector-verdict function (deriveConnectorDispatchInfo over the archived-aware summaries endpoint) feeds every strip, roster row, KPI, and detail header, so the timeline and roster can never disagree about who needs attention and archived identities are invisible everywhere except their collapsed history shelf. Every clause is a door: attention items link to the connector detail and say why (offline/degraded/reauth) in the verdict word, routing-rule rows land on the exact rule, and the trace spine (?trace=) keeps working end-to-end. Every lifecycle is closed in pixels: archive has an inline undo and a restore beside "history →", pause/run-now/disconnect/rotate-token live on the detail page with visible paused state and audit-door confirmation, so the backend's audit ledger and the screen describe the same set of possible actions. Nothing calm is unproven: every sub-query that fails names itself with a SourceDegradedNote instead of rendering "No incidents recorded", and "Policy lives in code" appears only after the rules fetch succeeded. On top of the already-strong ledger (honest hour totals, failed-status truth, saved views), that closes the gap to five-second verification: open /ingestion, and every quiet pixel is quiet because the system proved it.

findings.title: Deployments ledger has zero pixel readers; /system still answers "what code is running?" with a frozen v0.1.0 and a process-start proxy
findings.evidence: GET /api/system/deployments is live and truthful (git_sha 2136640..., migration_head mem_007, result success — verified via curl), shipped in bu-9r3hd.2 (commit 030bca85c, src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:398-431). But grep of frontend/src finds ZERO consumers: no API client function (frontend/src/api/client.ts has no deployment call), no hook in frontend/src/hooks/use-system.ts, no tile. Meanwhile VersionTile.tsx:82-98 renders "Package version 0.1.0" — a constant frozen in pyproject.toml:7 across ~115 commits — and labels started_at as "Last deploy" with a doc-admitted proxy comment (VersionTile.tsx:64-66). SystemVerdictBanner.tsx:192 composes the same vestigial "v0.1.0" into the all-clear verdict line.
findings.detail: Sin #6 (honesty mechanism shipped backend-only) + sin #8 (one fact, many numbers: "Last deploy" = process start-time proxy while deployments.finished_at is the enforced/actual value one endpoint away). The deploy spine's whole point was making the running-code question answerable in five seconds; on /system it still is not. The migration-drift tile can say "drifted" but the owner cannot see WHICH sha/migration-head is deployed without curl.

findings.title: Weekly restore drill is structurally starved: sleep-first in-process timer resets on every restart, so on this deploy cadence the drill never runs
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/backup_health.py:293-325 — run_restore_drill_loop does `await asyncio.sleep(interval_s)` FIRST with DEFAULT_RESTORE_DRILL_INTERVAL_S = 7*24*3600 (line 84), and the timer lives only in the api process (asyncio task in app.py:385). Any process restart resets the 7-day clock to zero; nothing anchors the schedule to the ledger's last checked_at. Live: restore_drill = {checked_at: null, result: 'pending'} (GET /api/system/backups), process started 2026-07-11T04:22 (uptime 13h), and the fleet merged ~115 commits in 2 days — deploys/restarts far more frequent than weekly. Consequence: 'restore drill never run' (SystemVerdictBanner.tsx:159-161) is a permanent banner resident.
findings.detail: Sin #9 — a lifecycle that stalls at the last step: the drill ledger, the honest 'pending' state, and the banner clause all shipped (bu-9r3hd.5), but the mechanism that would ever produce a real drill result cannot fire under real deploy cadence. The sleep-first rationale in the docstring ('avoids a real restore attempt at every process boot') is correct locally but fatal without persistence: correct design reads last restore_drill_result from public.audit_log on boot and runs after a short grace when >7d overdue, else sleeps the remainder. Same audit applies to any future long-interval in-process loop (hourly drift/deadman loops are immune — restarts shorter than their interval are rare).

findings.title: Data Egress catalog counts the entire audit log: 1.2M internal actions rendered as an external actor "Other / Unrecognized" — 99.1% of the ownership catalog is noise impersonating egress
findings.evidence: Live GET /api/system/egress: actors[0] = {actor_id: 'other', display_name: 'Other / Unrecognized', total_calls: 1,197,271, data_types: []} vs 9,450 Anthropic + 434 Telegram + 22 Google Calendar (real egress = 0.8%). Mechanism: system.py:968-983 aggregates ALL of public.audit_log by action; _ACTOR_REGISTRY (system.py:326-334) maps only 4 genuine egress operations (llm_api_call, telegram_send, google_calendar_write, gmail_send); every other audit action — pause/run-now audits, dashboard actions, breaker resets, drill results, all internal telemetry — falls into the 'other' bucket (system.py:1011-1014) and is presented under the tile heading "External services that received data" (EgressCatalogTile.tsx:31).
findings.detail: Inverse of sin #1: internal activity fabricated INTO an external-egress claim, with real-data authority. The owner's single privacy instrument answers its own question — 'who received my data?' — with 'mostly: unrecognized', which is both false (those 1.2M calls left nothing) and signal-drowning (the 4 real actors render below a meaningless million-count row). audit_log actions are a closed, enumerable vocabulary; egress-ness should be an attribute of the action taxonomy, not a 4-entry allowlist with a slop bucket.

findings.title: The verdict banner's all-clear is unreachable on the real deployment: static dev-posture booleans + the starved restore drill permanently occupy "N things need you"
findings.evidence: Live GET /api/health: insecure_infra_defaults=true, role_enforcement_disabled=true — both static process-lifetime config states (SecurityPostureTile.tsx:147-153 even labels the latter "Disabled (dev posture)"; security doctrine sets the trust boundary at network level, so these are standing accepted posture, not incidents). SystemVerdictBanner.tsx:164-170 pushes them into the problems list unconditionally, alongside the never-clearing 'restore drill never run' (lines 159-161, see finding 2). Net: the live /system opens with "3 things need you" every day, forever, and a NEW acute incident (drift, offline butler, corrupt backup) only changes the count from 3 to 4.
findings.detail: Earned-calm inversion: the doctrine says failure must never impersonate health, but the dual is that permanent, unactionable amber trains the owner to stop reading the banner — the five-second verification degrades to re-reading a list to diff it against yesterday's. The banner needs a standing-posture vs acute-incident split: chronic by-design states render as a quiet standing clause (still visible, honest, ideally owner-acknowledged via a decision bead per the new decision desk), while "things need you" is reserved for states that changed and are actionable. Note bu-gcz9e (in-flight) covers the DASHBOARD briefing's verdict, not this /system banner.

findings.title: Insight delivery-state endpoint returns zeros-as-HTTP-200 on ANY exception with no availability flag — a genuine DB failure impersonates "no delivery activity yet"
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:1221-1226: `except Exception as exc: logger.warning(...); return ApiResponse(data=_zero_state)` — a bare except that conflates pre-migration table absence with dropped connections/permission/timeout failures, exactly the classification the fleet-wide convention forbids (CLAUDE.md 'Classify before flagging', reference classifier memory.py::_is_missing_memory_schema_error). InsightDeliveryState has no available/degraded field; InsightDeliveryTile.tsx:97,108-110 renders the zeros as the documented honest empty state ('No deliveries yet'), and SystemVerdictBanner.tsx:127-133 only flags failed>0, so the failure also silently exits the verdict.
findings.detail: New instance of sin #2 on a surface the degraded-flag consumption batch (bu-jad4j/bu-tpudw) never touched. Compounding: the pipeline also has no staleness clause — live state is queued=69, delivered=23, last delivery 17h ago; if the delivery cron dies the queue grows while failed stays 0 (it counts only 3-strike filtered candidates) and both tile and banner stay calm. (Cron-staleness generally is known-deferred in the 07-10 dossier; the zeros-on-exception envelope violation here is new and independently fixable.)

findings.title: backup_history is fetched and discarded: 14 days of size-trend evidence (669MB→789MB, ~9MB/day growth) invisible; DbSizeTile shows a point-in-time number only
findings.evidence: GET /api/system/backups returns backup_history (14 dated size/status rows; live data shows monotonic growth 669,534,931 → 789,647,572 bytes over 7 days) but the only frontend references are test fixtures (grep: frontend/src/pages/SystemPage.test.tsx only); BackupTile.tsx renders status/recency/drill and never the history. DbSizeTile similarly renders current pg_database_size with no trend or time-to-disk-pressure clause.
findings.detail: Missed judgment-layer opportunity rather than a dishonesty: the instrument holds the exact series needed to answer 'is my database growing unsustainably?' (a real ownership fact — ~2.7GB/year at current rate) and throws it away. A 7-point sparkline plus a growth-rate clause turns two static tiles into a leading indicator. Also worth folding in: banner problem lines for same-page tiles (posture, backups, drift, insights) have no href/anchor (SystemVerdictBanner.tsx:220-229), so the door contract stops one hop short — an anchor + highlight to the owning tile completes it cheaply.

audits.jarvis_gap: The page's honesty machinery is real and largely exemplary — live-computed drift, verified backup artifacts, canonical shared liveness, three-way states on every tile, a verdict banner that refuses premature all-clear — but the verdict it composes cannot be trusted as a five-second instrument: its all-clear is structurally unreachable (static dev-posture + a restore drill whose weekly in-process timer can never survive the deploy cadence), its ownership catalog is 99% internal noise wearing an external-egress label, and the deploy spine's own ledger — the answer to \"what code is running?\" — has zero pixels while a frozen v0.1.0 stands in its place.
audits.ideal: The ideal /system opens with a verdict that is actually earnable: one line that is green only when every mechanism below has PROVEN health, with chronic accepted posture (network-only auth, dev role enforcement) folded into a quiet standing-posture clause the owner has explicitly acknowledged via a decision bead — so \"2 things need you\" always means two NEW, actionable things, each line an anchor-door to its owning tile. The Version tile becomes a Deployment tile reading the deployments ledger: short git sha (linking to the commit), migration head vs codebase head (same comparison the drift tile makes, one source), deploy result, and a recent-deploys drawer — the running-code question answered in one glance. The backup card carries the full chain of custody: last artifact verified (gzip-checked live), restore drill anchored to the ledger (runs on boot when >7d overdue, so it actually fires), and a size sparkline from backup_history with a growth-rate clause. The egress catalog enumerates only operations that genuinely leave the machine, each with data types and a coverage statement (\"classified N of M audited external operations\"), so the privacy instrument's biggest row is never \"Unrecognized\". Every aggregate that can fail carries an availability flag with a pixel reader, per the fleet convention — including insight delivery, which also gets a pipeline-staleness clause so a dead cron cannot render as calm.

moves.title: Standing-posture vs acute-incident split in the /system verdict (owner-acknowledged posture)
moves.why: The all-clear is unreachable: static by-design dev-posture booleans sit in 'N things need you' forever, so the banner degrades from a verdict into a list the owner must diff by memory — chronic amber trains dismissal, which is how a real incident gets missed.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Classify problem sources as acute (offline, drift, corrupt artifact, failed drill, source errors) vs standing (posture booleans, accepted-config states). 2) Standing states render as one quiet muted clause under the banner ('standing posture: network-only auth, dev role enforcement — accepted <date>'), excluded from the count; all-clear line becomes reachable and composes over acute sources only. 3) Acknowledgement is an owner decision: seed a decision bead (Decision Desk convention) per standing state; unacknowledged standing states still count as acute until decided. 4) Give every same-page problem line an anchor href + tile highlight to complete the door contract.
moves.integration_points: SystemVerdictBanner.tsx:164-175,189-232, SecurityPostureTile, /decisions desk convention (bu-ckkpz), GET /api/health posture fields.

moves.title: Honest insight-delivery envelope: availability flag + pipeline-staleness clause
moves.why: A bare except returns zeros-as-200 with no flag, so a genuine DB failure renders as the documented 'honest empty state' — a textbook new instance of the classify-before-flagging violation on a surface the degraded-flag sweep never reached; and a dead delivery cron reads as calm because only 3-strike failures count as problems.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Classify the exception (UndefinedTableError → legitimate zero state; anything else → available:false) per the memory.py reference classifier; add `available: bool` to InsightDeliveryState. 2) Tile renders the named degraded note (SourceDegradedNote vocabulary) when unavailable; banner adds 'insight delivery state unavailable'. 3) Staleness clause: queued>0 AND last_delivery_at older than ~2 delivery cycles → 'insight queue stalled (69 queued, last delivery 17h ago)' problem line. 4) Contract test in the degraded-envelope suite + FE flag-consumption registry entry.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:1219-1243, InsightDeliveryTile.tsx, SystemVerdictBanner.tsx:127-133, tests/contracts degraded-envelope suite (bu-tpudw.5 registry).

moves.title: Growth-trend clause: backup_history sparkline + days-to-pressure on DB size
moves.why: The endpoint already ships 14 days of dated size points (669→789MB) that the UI throws away; rendering the trend converts two static tiles into the leading indicator the ownership page should be ('growing ~9MB/day').
moves.slice_plan: 1) Sparkline (existing chart primitives, dataviz-compliant) + delta clause in BackupTile from backup_history. 2) DbSizeTile gains a growth-rate line derived from the same series (backup size ≈ DB size proxy) or a small persisted size sample. 3) Alert nothing — trend is elaboration, not a verdict source, until a real threshold exists.
moves.integration_points: BackupTile.tsx, DbSizeTile.tsx, frontend/src/api/types BackupFacts.backup_history (already typed).

audits.movement_claim: n/a — first dedicated audit of /system; deploy-spine mechanisms verified real on this pass (drift computed live per request at system.py:465, drill/drift loops actually wired in app.py:333/385, backup artifact status live-verified), but two of its guarantees (deployments visibility, restore drill ever firing) stop one step short of true.

audits.jarvis_gap: The one-command-spine is real and new surfaces are now born speaking it (DecisionsPage shipped with j/k triage, footer hints, degraded-aware empty; Chronicles registered palette verbs + [/]/t bindings) — but a world-class shell never advertises a dead shortcut, gives its three attention queues (approvals/decisions/qa, the badge-bearing five-second-verification doors) direct g-chords, teaches navigation chords in the palette itself (not only the '?' sheet), and ends every backend trace spine in a door: today the whole shortcut layer silently dies while the floating chat is open, and the deploy ledger is reachable only by curl.
audits.movement_claim: improved — the 07-10 registries were adopted, not drifted from: /decisions was born keyboard-first with honest empty/degraded states, and Chronicles wired its date-nav verbs into both the palette and the '?' sheet; the one major finding is a latent cross-mechanism defect that predates the baseline, not a regression.

findings.title: Open floating chat panel silently suspends every page-scoped keyboard shortcut app-wide
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-register-shortcut.tsx:147 — isShortcutTargetSuspended() returns true whenever ANY '[role="dialog"]' exists in the DOM; frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:349-354 renders a persistent, NON-modal role="dialog" (no aria-modal, no scrim, fixed bottom-right, docstring: "reachable from every dashboard route, mounted once in RootLayout.tsx" — it stays open while the owner browses and triages). While the chat panel is open, every useRegisterShortcut binding is suspended: Approvals j/k/a/d/x/u, Decisions/Issues/Dashboard/Notifications j/k (use-list-triage.ts routes through useRegisterShortcut), Chronicles [/]/t, Sessions and Calendar bindings — with zero indication. Worse, the '?' help sheet (shortcut-hints.tsx:62-68, "On this page") still advertises the dead bindings, since useShortcutHintEntries reads the registry, not the suspension state. g-chords and Cmd+K keep working (separate handler in use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts), making the failure look like random per-page breakage.
findings.detail: The suspension comment at use-register-shortcut.tsx:145-147 only anticipated modal overlays (EntityFinder, '?' sheet, useModalChoreography overlays); the chat widget is a non-modal dialog designed for concurrent use — chatting WHILE triaging is the widget's whole point (page-context capture exists precisely for that). Fix mechanism, not symptom: suspend only for (a) an open MODAL dialog anywhere — query '[role="dialog"][aria-modal="true"]', which every real modal in the codebase already sets (EntityFinder.tsx:548-549, ButlerManagementTab, CalendarAgendaView, Radix Dialog/Sheet) and the chat widget correctly does not — plus (b) event targets contained INSIDE any dialog (so typing/tabbing within the chat panel never triggers page verbs). One-line predicate change + a regression test in use-register-shortcut.test.tsx with a non-modal dialog mounted.

findings.title: The three badge-bearing attention queues (/approvals, /decisions, /qa) have no g-chords while low-traffic pages do; chord assignment has no convention
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/layout/nav-config.ts:72-75 — the only three routes with badgeKey (qa-escalations red, approvals-pending amber, decisions-open amber) all lack a chord field, while Audit Log (chord 'a', line 106), Ingestion ('e'), and Contacts ('c', route-registry.ts:75) have them. Letters d, p, q are unassigned in G_CHORD_ROUTES (used set: o b e m h t n i s a c). /spend (line 105) also shipped nav-visible with no chord.
findings.detail: These are exactly the destinations the north star's five-second verification loop visits when a badge lights up — the tenth use is 'badge appeared → go decide' and today that hop is mouse-or-palette only. Distinct from the standing known (10/13 VERB scopes lack bindings): this is navigation-chord coverage. Mechanism: a chord-coverage convention enforced in route-registry.test.ts — any sidebar route declaring badgeKey MUST declare a chord (a badge is a claim on attention; attention deserves a direct key) — then assign g-p (Approvals), g-d (Decisions), g-q (QA), optionally g-$ or g-u for Spend. New pages then cannot be born chord-less if they carry a badge.

findings.title: Palette Pages rows never advertise their g-chords — the binding-teaching column exists but was generalized only to Actions
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/layout/EntityFinder.tsx:89-93 — ALL_PAGES maps route-registry entries down to {label, path, section}, discarding the chord field the registry carries; the Pages group render (EntityFinder.tsx:790-812) has no kbd column, while Actions rows (EntityFinder.tsx:922-931) render PaletteCommand.binding via KbMono (bu-qvnce.11). The only place g-chords are taught is the '?' help sheet (shortcut-hints.tsx:33-42).
findings.detail: The codebase's own doctrine (command-registry.tsx:47-53, discoverability bar: 'the palette is where shortcuts are learned') says each entry's keybinding shows inline — a user who reaches Approvals through the palette three times a day is never nudged to the two-keystroke path. Mechanism already built once: carry chord through PageEntry and render ['g', chord] with the exact same KbMono column the Actions group uses — ~10 lines, and it makes move 2's new chords self-teaching on day one.

findings.title: Deployments ledger has no door — GET /api/system/deployments is live with data and has zero frontend consumers
findings.evidence: Live: curl http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/system/deployments returns {current: {git_sha: 2136640…, migration_head: mem_007, result: "success", …}, recent: […]}. Source: rg 'deployments' frontend/src → zero non-test hits; frontend/src/pages/SystemPage.tsx:112-128 renders VersionTile (GET /api/system/instance — version + started_at only, VersionTile.tsx:5-6) and DriftTile (GET /api/system/drift) but nothing reads the bu-9r3hd.2 ledger.
findings.detail: The deploy spine (bu-9r3hd, all five children landed) ends one hop short of the owner: 'what sha is running, when did it ship, did the deploy SUCCEED' is answerable only by curl — and a deployments row with result='failure' would impersonate health everywhere in the UI, since DriftTile only covers Alembic-head drift and VersionTile shows a version string with no success/failure or history. The live stack demonstrates the stakes: the deployed sha (2136640) predates the /decisions merge, so the FE currently 404s on /api/decisions — a deploy-lag state the /system page cannot explain today. Fix: a DeploymentsTile on /system (current sha shortened + migration_head + result clause, red on failure; recent-deploys list as a drawer/door), plus a SystemVerdictBanner clause when the latest deployment failed or when running sha ≠ origin/main (the drift sentinel already computes the raw material).

moves.title: Scope shortcut suspension to modal dialogs only (aria-modal predicate + containment check)
moves.why: One selector change un-kills the entire page-shortcut layer while the floating chat is open — the shell's keyboard spine currently has a global off-switch nobody can see, and the '?' sheet advertises bindings that are dead.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-register-shortcut.tsx:135-149 (isShortcutTargetSuspended); regression test alongside existing use-register-shortcut tests with a mounted non-modal role=dialog; verify every real modal sets aria-modal (EntityFinder.tsx:548-549 already does; ButlerManagementTab, CalendarAgendaView, Radix Dialog/Sheet do).
moves.slice_plan: Single slice: change querySelector to '[role=\"dialog\"][aria-modal=\"true\"]', add target-inside-dialog containment (el.closest('[role=\"dialog\"]')) so chat-internal keys never leak to the page, add tests for (a) chat-open + j fires page verb when focus is on page, (b) focus inside chat suspends, (c) open modal still suspends all.

moves.title: Chord-coverage convention: badgeKey ⇒ chord, enforced by test; assign g-p/g-d/g-q
moves.why: The badge-bearing attention queues are the five-second-verification doors; a badge is a claim on attention and today its destination has no direct key while Audit Log does.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/layout/nav-config.ts:72-75 (add chord fields), frontend/src/lib/route-registry.test.ts (new invariant: every route with badgeKey declares a chord; chords unique), shortcut-hints.tsx picks them up automatically via ALL_ROUTES.
moves.slice_plan: One slice: add chords p/d/q (+optionally Spend), add the registry test, confirm no collisions with page-scoped single-key bindings (g-prefix makes them collision-free by construction).

moves.title: Render g-chords on palette Pages rows via the existing KbMono binding column
moves.why: The palette is where shortcuts are learned (the codebase's own doctrine); the teaching mechanism was built for Actions in bu-qvnce.11 and never generalized to the group that has had registry-carried bindings all along.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/layout/EntityFinder.tsx:83-93 (PageEntry gains chord), :790-812 (Pages group renders ['g', chord] with the same KbMono column as :922-931), EntityFinder tests.
moves.slice_plan: One slice with move 2 (lands the new chords self-teaching): thread chord through ALL_PAGES, render kbd column when present, snapshot test.

moves.title: Deployments door on /system: DeploymentsTile + failed-deploy verdict clause
moves.why: Closes the last hop of the shipped deploy spine — deploy success/failure and running-sha history must be a door in the instrument, not a curl endpoint; a failed deploy today impersonates health in every UI surface.
moves.integration_points: New frontend/src/components/system/DeploymentsTile.tsx consuming GET /api/system/deployments (add client fn + types in frontend/src/api/, hook in hooks/use-system.ts); mount in SystemPage.tsx:112-128 grid beside VersionTile/DriftTile; SystemVerdictBanner clause for latest result != success; degraded-envelope handling per CLAUDE.md convention.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: API client + hook + tile (current sha/migration_head/result, red failure clause, recent-deploys disclosure list). Slice 2: verdict-banner clause + e2e/a11y tests; consider retiring VersionTile's started_at into the tile to keep one deploy-truth surface.

audits.ideal: A shell where the command spine is total and truthful: every destination and verb reachable by keyboard from anywhere, with exactly one registry feeding sidebar, palette, g-chords, and the '?' sheet (already true); where a shortcut that is advertised always fires (suspension scoped to genuinely modal contexts), where attention-badged queues each own a two-keystroke chord the palette itself teaches inline, and where every backend trace spine — including deploys — terminates in a visible door so nothing about the system's own state is curl-only.

audits.jarvis_gap: The token/lint machinery built by bu-86c4c.5/.6 measurably works (fallbacks down 165→134, focus-visible 2→53 files, skeleton-pulse eliminated, ~1,378 muted-foreground sites snapped to AA via aliasing) — but the newest flagship surface (chronicles IEA) shipped its own 9-hex non-theming palette through an enforcement blind spot (.ts files exempt from the hex guard), and new components dodge the state-color-fill rule via bg-[var(--red)] arbitrary values the guard doesn't match, so the language still cannot defend itself against pages being born off-Dispatch.
audits.movement_claim: improved — three of four standing knowns moved the right way (wrong-value var() fallbacks 165→134, focus-visible adoption 2→53 files, skeleton-pulse removed entirely from ui/skeleton.tsx and guarded by ANIMATE_PULSE_SELECTORS), though stock solid-badge-fill files grew 13→17 (StreakCallouts, ConflictRadarBanner, HourFlameStrip, ButlerChroniclerTimelinesTab added) and the two type scales (index.css 1.2-ratio --text-* vs the Dispatch px table) both still exist.

findings.title: Chronicles lane palette is a second, untokenized, non-theming color system (9 raw hexes in a .ts file the hex-guard cannot see)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/lane-taxonomy.ts:92-158 defines 9 raw hexes (#64748b, #f43f5e, #2563eb, #7c3aed, #ec4899, #06b6d4, #f59e0b, #059669, #94a3b8) plus parallel stock Tailwind classes (bg-rose-500, bg-blue-600, ...) kept in sync only by the comment 'Must visually match colour above' (lines 66-72). These are static: dark mode renders the same saturated hexes while every other categorical ramp in index.css:530-542 is deliberately chroma-muted for the dark-primary 'evening-glance' commitment — and chronicles is the evening-review surface. TrendsLens.tsx:165 colors TEXT with these hexes directly (#f59e0b amber on light --bg ≈ 2:1, the exact AA failure --amber-text was created to fix per index.css:136-140). Enforcement gap: eslint.config.js:337-346 applies only HSL_VAR+STATUS_COLOR+ANIMATE_PULSE to **/*.ts — HEX_COLOR_SELECTORS (line 96, 'banned in JSX files') is .tsx-only, so a palette defined in a .ts module sails through; and the STATUS_COLOR regex (line 61) only covers red/green/emerald/amber/yellow/orange, so bg-blue-600/bg-rose-500/bg-cyan-500/bg-slate-500 are unguarded everywhere. The file header (lines 14-21) justifies not using --category-* by claiming the ramp is 'reserved for butler letter-marks only', which contradicts both index.css:80-83 ('General categorical palette for groups, labels, tags') and chart-colors.ts's category channel doc ('Non-butler categorical coloring ... hash-slotted across the same --category-1..12 ramp', consumed by relationship/ContactTable.tsx:79 et al.) — doctrine §Butler hue scope (design-language.md:936-944) constrains butler-assigned hues, not the token ramp.
findings.detail: Unifying mechanism: promote the lane palette to named --lane-sleep..--lane-other tokens in index.css with light AND dark values chroma-tuned to the categorical ramp (~0.12-0.14), forward via @theme inline, and give SVG/WebGL consumers the same treatment hex-heatmap.ts already got in bu-qvnce.7 (computed literals cross-checked against index.css by a test). Delete the colour/hex dual encoding from LaneConfig. Extend HEX_COLOR_SELECTORS to **/*.ts and widen STATUS_COLOR_SELECTORS to all stock Tailwind palette hues (or replace with a 'stock palette class' ban plus token allowlist).

findings.title: New-born components violate State Color Discipline with solid state-color background fills, dodging the lint guard via bg-[var(--red)] arbitrary values
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/system/DriftTile.tsx:112 ('bg-[var(--green)] text-white ... rounded-full' pill for 'no drift') and :130 ('bg-[var(--red)] text-white' pill) — born 07-11 under landed bu-9r3hd.1. Spec §State Color Discipline: state colors 'never on background fills — foreground or border only', sole exception the 4-7% .attention-row tint+rail; a solid green celebration chip for a healthy state also breaches quiet-success ('no green-check moments', §Interface Copy). The eslint STATUS_COLOR guard only matches raw Tailwind shade classes (bg-red-500 style, eslint.config.js:61), so bg-[var(--red)] passes clean. Same family: components/calendar/ConflictRadarBanner.tsx:126 ships a 'bg-emerald-600 ... text-white hover:bg-emerald-700' Accept-fix button behind an eslint-disable whose justification ('call-to-action button color (confirm affordance)') is precisely what the exemption doc says is NOT exempt — §Button Forms mandates the commit form (--fg bg / --bg text, 'never colored') for committing actions. components/chronicles/StreakCallouts.tsx:81 renders solid saturated rounded-full lane-colored pills with text-white ('icon-and-label chips floating in space' + celebration, both on the §Anti-Pattern list); components/ingestion/timeline/HourFlameStrip.tsx:213 introduces unguarded bg-blue-500 for the replay series.
findings.detail: Mechanism, not symptoms: add selectors for /\b(?:bg|from|via|to|fill)-\[var\(--(?:red|amber|green|severity-)/ to the guard so token-referencing fills are caught too; convert DriftTile pills to StateDot + plain text, ConflictRadarBanner to the commit-button form, StreakCallouts to muted kind tags; audit the 13 existing no-restricted-syntax disables for justification drift (12 are legitimate categorical exemptions; ConflictRadarBanner's is not).

findings.title: DayNarrative renders LLM-composed prose as sans body with no source-honesty affordance — the system's voice is bilingual within a single page
findings.evidence:
frontend/src/components/chronicles/DayNarrative.tsx:74-80 renders the chronicler's once-daily LLM prose summary (header comment lines 2-8 confirms it is 'LLM prose') as

— sans, 14px. Spec §Type System: Source Serif 4 is 'the system's voice — LLM-written elaborations'; §Voice Surface reserves the serif register for exactly this. Sibling component RecentDaysIndex.tsx:96-98 on the same Chronicles page correctly uses fontFamily: var(--font-serif) + italic. Additionally §Process Status Pill: 'The system SHALL report on its own process (briefing source, cache age ...) via the tiny 9px mono status pill ... always honest about what is rendering' — DayNarrative renders LLM output visually indistinguishable from system chrome, with no source/age affordance (the Overview briefing has one).
findings.detail: Fix: render dayNarrative in the Voice register (serif roman, 16px/1.6, max-width 50ch) and attach the shared process-status pill stating the labeling pass's day/source; sweep other LLM-prose surfaces (episode narration, gap-interview copy) for the same sans-voice drift.

findings.title: Attention-tint pattern hand-rolled outside .attention-row with out-of-bounds alpha and stacked affordances
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/approvals/attention-ledger-panel.tsx:59-68 builds a red alert box as 'border-[var(--red)]/40 bg-[var(--red)]/10' plus a solid red dot plus red text; :177-183 the same in amber at /10. Doctrine's attention-tint exception (design-language.md §Attention-tint exception, implemented index.css:677-684) bounds the tint at red 4-7% / amber 4-6% alpha, requires the 2px left rail ('tint + rail travel together as a single signal unit'), and forbids a second affordance on the same row — this new component (landed bu-tdd4k.4) uses 10% alpha, a rounded box instead of the rail, and three stacked affordances (tint + dot + colored bold text).
findings.detail: Route both banners through the existing .attention-row class (or a shared <AttentionNote tone="red|amber"> wrapper over it) so the alpha bounds and one-affordance rule are structural; the degraded branch should reuse SourceDegradedNote like every other fan-out surface.

findings.title: Eyebrow primitive exists but even born-Dispatch 07-10..12 surfaces hand-roll three divergent eyebrow dialects
findings.evidence: components/ui/Eyebrow.tsx is canonical (font-mono text-[10px] uppercase tracking-[0.14em], per spec §Eyebrow Section Titles). New surfaces ignore it: pages/DecisionsPage.tsx:196 and components/approvals/attention-ledger-panel.tsx:138,189 use tracking-widest (0.1em); components/chronicles/DayRibbon.tsx:129,162 and TrendsLens.tsx:156 use non-mono text-[10px] uppercase tracking-wider (0.05em); components/chronicles/EpisodeDrawer.tsx:355,417,445,458,518,566,578 and WorkScheduleSettings.tsx:400 use the pre-Dispatch text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider dialect. App-wide: 121 hand-tracked uppercase instances vs the one primitive.
findings.detail: Mechanism: eslint.config.js already has PRIMITIVE_REDECLARATION_SELECTORS — add a selector matching Literal[value=/uppercase.*tracking-(wide|wider|widest)/] outside components/ui/** with the message 'use <Eyebrow>'; codemod the 121 sites (most are mechanical).

findings.title: Chronicles SVG internals are theme-blind and reuse the state-red hue for a non-status marker
findings.evidence: components/chronicles/GanttSwimlaneInner.tsx:633 zebra lane fills use rgba(0,0,0,0.02/0.04) — black tint that vanishes on the canonical dark theme (dark-primary doctrine: 'when a trade-off is forced, the dark experience wins'), while the tick lines 20 lines below (:648-650) correctly use stroke="currentColor" strokeOpacity=0.08 — two techniques in one file. components/chronicles/MapWidgetInner.tsx:40,42 paints the playhead marker hsl(0 84% 60%) (≈ --red's hue) with a hardcoded white border — the error hue assigned a second meaning ('current position') as a raw literal; :180 trail line hsl(220 90% 56%) is another unnamed hue; the file header :12 still advertises the 'red→green palette' bu-qvnce.7 replaced with neutralDensityColor.
findings.detail: Zebra fills → currentColor + fillOpacity (matching the ticks); playhead → var(--fg) ring over the trail hue or a named --map-playhead token computed like NEUTRAL_DENSITY_* (WebGL cannot resolve var()); trail line joins the lane/token registry from the lane-palette move; fix the stale header.

findings.title: Phantom token var(--green-text) referenced — the text-safe state-color triad was never completed
findings.evidence: components/chronicles/BalanceRings.tsx:38 uses "var(--green-text, var(--green))" but --green-text is defined nowhere in frontend/src/index.css (only --amber-text at :140 and --red-text at :148 exist), so the fallback always wins — a new wrong-value-fallback instance created by pattern-completing a triad that has only two members. Light-mode --green (oklch 0.50 0.140 152) as small text is borderline against --bg-elev. Secondary: the delta vocabulary maps up→green / down→amber (:37-41), giving amber (spec meaning: 'medium severity, degraded') a second meaning of 'below your usual' on lanes where less is not degraded (less work, less travel).
findings.detail: Add --green-text to index.css in both themes (mirroring the bu-86c4c.16/bu-f310e split, with the contrast.test.ts cross-check) and drop the fallback; consider neutral +/- deltas (mono, --dim) for balance lanes since 'vs usual' is not a health signal.

audits.ideal: One color registry, mechanically defended: every hue in the app resolves to a named token in index.css (surfaces, three state colors + their text-safe variants, --category-1..12, --lane-1..9, chart-1..5, neutral density ramp), every consumer channel routes through chart-colors.ts or a ui/ primitive (Eyebrow, StateDot, KindTag, AttentionNote, commit/pill buttons), and the lint guards are symmetric — hex/stock-class/state-fill bans apply to .ts and .tsx alike and match bg-[var(--red)]-style arbitrary values, so a page cannot be born off-Dispatch. LLM prose always speaks in serif with a process-status pill; SVG/WebGL surfaces get their literals from tested oklch math pinned to the token file. The dispatch-kit page recipe plus these guards make conformance the path of least resistance rather than a review outcome.

findings.title: DayRibbon flashes a fabricated 'No activity recorded' empty on every day-step
findings.detail: The new IEA drilldown (bu-8whey5, landed 07-10) passes only `episodes` into DayRibbon; on each date navigation the episodes query re-keys, data is undefined, and DayRibbon renders its truthful-empty copy while the fetch is in flight. Every sibling widget on the same panel gates on loading (BalanceRings.tsx:129, WhoYouWereWithPanel.tsx:50, StreakCallouts.tsx:47, GanttSwimlane.tsx:118 `isLoading && episodes.length === 0`); DayRibbon has no isLoading prop at all. Live episode fetch is ~28ms + waterfall, so this is a visible ~100-300ms false-empty flash on the page's hottest interaction (prev/next day stepper) — the exact 'false empty' class the memory-registers known documents, reintroduced on a brand-new surface two days after the program shipped. Fix: thread isLoading (or the query object) into DayRibbon and gate the empty branch on !isLoading, plus the unifying convention below.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/DayRibbon.tsx:113-120 (`if (episodes.length === 0) { ... No activity recorded for this window. }`, no loading prop) vs ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:120-121 (episodes = episodesQuery.data?.data ?? []) and 226-231 (DayRibbon receives only episodes/window/onClick); siblings' loading gates at BalanceRings.tsx:129, WhoYouWereWithPanel.tsx:50, StreakCallouts.tsx:47, GanttSwimlane.tsx:118; live latency episodes=0.028s

findings.title: /decisions and the Attention Ledger panel shipped with zero update path — neither bus-covered nor poll-token polled
findings.detail: The fleet's triage-queue convention (approvals/issues/notifications/sessions) is bus invalidation + POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS reconciliation sweep. The two newest owner-attention surfaces follow neither: useDecisions() is a bare useQuery with no refetchInterval, and ["decisions"] appears nowhere in EVENT_CACHE_REGISTRY (registry keys: approval/spend/session/notification/issue/ingestion/header_delta/attention_*/heartbeat). Same for AttentionLedgerPanel's ["attention-ledger","summary"] — and pointedly, the bus's attention_add/attention_remove event types ARE received but routed to settingsConsoleDeltaPatch, an intentional no-op scoped to the settings-console reducer, so attention events flow through the socket while the attention ledger panel they describe stays stale. Once mounted, both surfaces update only on window refocus — on an always-open single-pane dashboard, a decision queue whose verdict line says 'N decisions waiting, oldest Xd' silently fossilizes. Neither file is in POLL_POLICY_FILES, so no lint catches it. This is the third consecutive run where a freshly-born surface missed the poll/bus convention — the mechanism, not the instances, is the finding.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-decisions.ts:13-18 (no refetchInterval, no poll token import); frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:194-205 (no decisions entry; attention_add/attention_remove -> settingsConsoleDeltaPatch no-op, comment at :172-183); frontend/src/components/approvals/attention-ledger-panel.tsx:122-125 (bare useQuery); frontend/eslint.config.js:221-229 (POLL_POLICY_FILES excludes both)

findings.title: Ingestion rule toggle is dead-feeling and repeat-unsafe — violates the codebase's own OPTIMISTIC classification doctrine
findings.detail: RuleRow's Switch is bound to server truth (`checked={rule.enabled}`) and handleToggleRule is a plain mutation with no onMutate, no isPending wiring, and no disable: the switch does not move until the PATCH succeeds AND the invalidated rules list refetches (two round trips), and nothing prevents firing concurrent PATCHes by flipping repeatedly during flight. use-optimistic-mutation.ts's own header doctrine (bu-86c4c.13) names 'toggles' as the canonical OPTIMISTIC class ('The owner should never see a spinner for these' — here there is not even a spinner, just a frozen control). Same unclassified-mutation class: use-timeline-saved-views.ts create/update/delete (pin/label-class actions) are plain invalidate-on-success. 8 hook files adopted the shared optimistic path; ~30 files still call raw useMutation with no mechanism forcing the OPTIMISTIC-vs-HONEST-PENDING classification the hook's doc demands.

findings.title: Chronicles drilldown skips the never-blank floor the top of its own page uses
findings.detail: ChroniclesPage's briefing column implements bu-nhcp5 correctly — placeholderData keeps the previous day's briefing visible and FetchingDim dims it during day-stepping (ChroniclesPage.tsx:326-337). But the drilldown below (the majority of the page: timeline, gantt, ribbon, rings, companions, trends, narrative — 8 queries keyed on date) has no placeholderData anywhere in use-chronicles.ts, so every prev/next-day step drops the entire lower page to skeletons (and DayRibbon to a false empty, finding 1) while the column above dims gracefully. All backing endpoints are <100ms live, so the previous day's content could stay up dimmed at near-zero cost. The day stepper is also perfectly predictable navigation — the adjacent day's briefing+episodes could be prefetched on stepper hover/idle via the existing prefetch-on-intent mechanism, which today only understands route pathnames (prefetch-registry matchers), not param/state navigations like ?date= or calendar entries.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-chronicles.ts (zero placeholderData across all 20 read hooks; grep confirms) vs frontend/src/pages/ChroniclesPage.tsx:326-337 (FetchingDim + placeholderData comment); frontend/src/components/chronicles/ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:113-183 (8 date-keyed queries); frontend/src/lib/prefetch-registry.ts (pathname-only matchers); live latencies: briefing 0.089s, balance 0.011s, trends 0.009s, episodes 0.028s

findings.title: Legacy AutoRefreshToggle 10s poll overrides the blessed bus+reconcile pattern on SessionsPage
findings.detail: use-sessions.ts is the flagship of the poll-policy convention (POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS defaults, bus sessionPatch coverage) — but SessionsPage itself defeats it: useAutoRefresh(10_000) is default-ENABLED and its refetchInterval is passed into four bus-covered queries, so the page hard-polls every 10s on top of bus invalidation. The toggle persists a localStorage preference (AUTO_REFRESH_ENABLED_KEY) that reads as global but is consumed by exactly two surfaces (SessionsPage, dashboard SessionStripeChart) — a user turning 'auto-refresh' off silences sessions while every other polled surface keeps its hardcoded interval. This predates the event bus and is now a second, contradictory freshness mechanism; it should be folded into (or deleted in favor of) the bus-aware interval policy bu-01r64.3 is building — the localStorage preference layer itself is outside that epic's scope.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SessionsPage.tsx:123 (useAutoRefresh(10_000)), :154-198 (refetchInterval: autoRefreshControl.refetchInterval on 4 queries) vs frontend/src/hooks/use-sessions.ts:45,69,80 (POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS defaults being overridden); frontend/src/hooks/use-auto-refresh.ts:13-15 (default enabled=true); consumers: only SessionsPage.tsx + SessionStripeChart.tsx:108

audits.ideal: Freshness and snappiness are system properties, not per-surface luck. Every query-key family in the app carries a machine-checked declaration of its update path — bus-covered (with its registry patch), named-poll-token (with the token stating primary-vs-reconcile intent), or static-by-design — and CI fails when a new hook ships undeclared, so a page like /decisions cannot be born stale. Every mutation site carries its optimism class: OPTIMISTIC actions (toggles, pins, acks, dismissals) go through the shared cancel→snapshot→apply→rollback path and never show a spinner; HONEST-PENDING actions wire isPending into the control they were triggered from. Navigation never blanks: the never-blank floor (placeholderData + FetchingDim) applies to every parameterized surface including param/state navigation (chronicles ?date=, calendar ?entry=), predictable next-steps (adjacent day, hovered row) are prefetched into the exact cache slot the destination reads, and no empty-state copy can render while its query is in flight. One freshness policy (bus health + poll tokens) replaces all legacy per-page refresh controls.
audits.jarvis_gap: The core mechanisms exist and are genuinely good — poll tokens, event-cache registry, prefetch-on-intent, never-blank floor, shared optimistic mutations — but each is enforced only where it was born: the two newest owner-attention surfaces (/decisions, IEA drilldown) shipped in the last 48h speaking none of them, proving the conventions are still tribal knowledge rather than fenced system properties; JARVIS never shows a fossilized decision queue or flashes 'no activity' at the owner mid-navigation.
audits.movement_claim: unchanged — the 07-10 program's mechanisms (POLL_RUNNING_SESSION_MS, RowLink prefetch wiring, degraded-note completion) held and matured, but the newest surfaces (/decisions, chronicles IEA drilldown) shipped off-pattern with zero update path and false-empty flashes, offsetting the gains; still solid, not yet self-enforcing.

findings.title: Gantt day timeline is invisible to assistive tech and pointer-only — svg role="img" swallows role="button" bars that have no keyboard path
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/GanttSwimlaneInner.tsx:601-602 (`<svg ... aria-label="Gantt timeline" role="img">`) wraps every episode bar rendered at :319-323 as `<g role="button" aria-label=... onClick={handleClick}>` with NO tabIndex and NO onKeyDown (grep for tabIndex/onKeyDown in the file returns zero hits). ARIA role="img" marks all descendants presentational, so the role="button" bars never reach the accessibility tree; and without tabIndex the click that opens the EpisodeDrawer evidence chain (bu-ig72b.31) is mouse-only. Live-confirmed lint blind spot: `npx eslint src/components/chronicles/GanttSwimlaneInner.tsx` exits clean despite jsx-a11y flatConfigs.recommended being enabled (eslint.config.js:257) — jsx-a11y's interactive-supports-focus/click-events-have-key-events only map HTML elements, not SVG `<g>`, so this class of defect is structurally unfenced. Contrast: DayRibbon.tsx:177-197, built the same week for the SAME panel (ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:204 vs :226), renders its activity blocks as real HTML <button>s with aria-label and focus-visible ring — two implementations of 'clickable episode block on a timeline' coexist, one accessible, one not.
findings.detail: The IEA redesign (bu-8whey5, 07-11) made the Chronicles drilldown the day-story centerpiece, and both the Gantt and the ribbon are doors onto the evidence chain — but for keyboard/SR users the Gantt door does not exist at all. Fix: drop role="img" from the bar SVG (or keep it aria-hidden and overlay HTML buttons like DayRibbon does), add tabIndex={0} + Enter/Space on each bar, and add the Chronicles drilldown to axe coverage. The systemic lesson: SVG interactivity is outside jsx-a11y's reach, so the repo needs either a 'no onClick on SVG elements without tabIndex+keyhandler' no-restricted-syntax selector or a single shared interactive-SVG pattern.

findings.title: title= tooltips regressed one day after the bu-sywxz Tip sweep, and the sweep left standing load-bearing sites — no lint fence exists

DayRibbon.tsx:149-153 (landed 07-11, 160ce8ca7) puts each planned/intent block's ONLY exposed info (title + duration) in a raw title= on a non-focusable <div> — pointer-only; the intent track's single aria-label (:135) names the track, not the blocks, so the plan-vs-reality comparison the ribbon exists for is absent for keyboard/SR users. findings.detail: The Tip primitive (components/ui/tip.tsx) is well built — focus-openable, SR-announced, asChild keeps one interactive node. What is missing is the mechanism: a no-restricted-syntax selector `JSXAttribute[name.name="title"]` scoped to host elements (message: use Tip, or eslint-disable with a reason for genuinely supplementary cases), plus finishing the sweep at the cited sites and pairing every opacity-0 group-hover reveal with group-focus-within.

findings.title: New ContactPeoplePicker autocomplete (bu-hzi4v, 07-11) ships without the combobox contract — no state semantics, no announcements, no arrow-key path
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/calendar/ContactPeoplePicker.tsx:119-127 — the Input carries no role="combobox", aria-expanded, aria-controls, or aria-autocomplete; the results <ul> (:139-172) is not a listbox and appears/disappears silently; 'Searching…' (:173-176) and 'No matches.' (:177-181) render with no aria-live/status region, so a screen-reader user typing a name gets zero feedback that matches exist; there is no ArrowDown path from the input into the results (results are Tab-reachable buttons only), and Enter in the input falls through to the surrounding dialog form instead of picking the top match.
findings.detail: This is the 'built once, never generalized' pattern in reverse: the repo has Radix primitives and a command palette but no shared Combobox/typeahead primitive, so the first new autocomplete since the a11y push was hand-rolled from Input + <ul>. Mechanism: add ui/combobox.tsx implementing the APG combobox pattern (aria-activedescendant roving, aria-expanded, polite status region announcing result counts), rebuild ContactPeoplePicker on it, and make it the mandated base for future pickers (secrets/entity search are next likely consumers).

findings.title: QA overview butler multi-select is a hand-rolled role="menu" with no menu keyboard behavior while ui/dropdown-menu.tsx sits unused beside it

findings.title: DecisionsPage rows are disclosures with no exposed state — selection/expansion is invisible to AT, and the expanded dossier lives inside the <button>

Worth folding the corrected shape back into the useListTriage exemplar docs since new triage pages copy ApprovalsPage/DecisionsPage verbatim.

audits.jarvis_gap: JARVIS never requires a mouse: every clause is a door reachable from the keyboard and audible to assistive tech. audits.ideal: Every interactive element in the dashboard is reachable, visible, and named from the keyboard alone, enforced by mechanism not memory: jsx-a11y plus repo-specific no-restricted-syntax fences (title= on host elements, onClick on SVG without tabIndex+keyhandler), one shared Combobox and one shared interactive-timeline pattern that all pickers and swimlanes are built from, hover-reveal always paired with focus-within reveal, disclosure/selection state always mirrored into aria-expanded/aria-current, and the axe route sweep burning down instead of frozen — so a new page cannot ship less accessible than the last one.
