findings.title: Roadmap candidate 1 designs recurring manual toil in while Gmail already captures bank-statement PDFs
findings.evidence: docs/plans/2026-07-10-connector-roadmap-proposal.md §3.3 (lines 116-137) specifies a manual drop-folder as the finance statement feed and never mentions the shipped Gmail attachment pipeline: src/butlers/connectors/gmail.py ATTACHMENT_POLICY already lazy-captures application/pdf up to 15MB and text/csv up to 10MB into switchboard.attachment_refs (docs/connectors/attachment-handling.md:14-33), meaning SG bank e-statement emails ALREADY land as fetchable attachment metadata on every statement cycle. The roadmap itself notes 'the owner already receives' the statement (line 115-116) yet routes capture through a hand-download step. A deterministic triage rule (bank-sender allowlist + application/pdf → eager fetch → candidate 1's PDF→CSV extractor → the existing bulk-transaction-ingestion composite-dedup path, openspec/specs/bulk-transaction-ingestion/spec.md) makes the same pipeline zero-touch; the drop-folder should be the fallback for statements that arrive only via bank-portal login, not the primary path.
findings.detail: Same PDF→CSV extraction work either way; the difference is whether the owner performs a monthly download ritual forever. The attachment doc's 'Structured HTML Extraction (Future)' extension point (attachment-handling.md:51-53) is the designed-in hook for exactly this class of sender-specific extraction.

findings.title: Travel manifesto makes a binding promise (delay/gate alerts 'before the airlines announce them') with zero flight-status capture behind it
findings.evidence: roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md: 'We will alert you to delays and gate changes before the airlines announce them' and 'Get notified of changes — when your flight is rescheduled, cancelled, or delayed, you know before you check your email.' No flight-status connector or API integration exists anywhere (grep of src/butlers/connectors/, openspec/specs/ — no flight/status surface); RFC 0018 defers flight tracking as P2 paid (0018:138 'AeroAPI ~$1/query; booking confirmations already arrive via Gmail'). Gmail-only capture can never beat the airline's own announcement. vision.md rule 6 makes manifestos binding: 'A capability that contradicts it must not be added without a formal amendment' — the inverse also holds: a promise with no capability is a doctrine violation. The 07-10 connector roadmap scanned only four domains (money/attention/food/work) and never audited manifesto promises against capture reality, so travel was missed entirely.
findings.detail: Two honest exits: (a) a trip-window-gated status poller — travel.legs already has type='flight', departure_at, arrival_at, carrier, pnr (roster/travel/migrations/001_travel_tables.py:53-71), so polling only inside T-48h..arrival bounds a paid API to ~dozens of calls per trip; or (b) amend the manifesto to stop promising pre-announcement alerts. Either closes the gap; the status quo (promise without substrate) is the one non-option.

findings.title: Roadmap candidate 4a measures inbound work noise, not the owner's work output — GitHub self-activity generates no notification email
findings.evidence: docs/plans/2026-07-10-connector-roadmap-proposal.md §7.1-7.4 builds the work digest exclusively over switchboard.email_metadata_refs (GitHub-via-email). GitHub does not email you about your own pushes/PRs/reviews — notification email covers watched-repo activity by others. So the proposed digest's '14 PRs touched' rollup systematically undercounts the strongest workday signal: the owner's authored activity. The free GitHub Events API (GET /users/{login}/events, PAT-authenticated, ETag-conditional) yields authored commits/PRs/reviews with timestamps at zero cost, fitting the same nightly-aggregate/no-per-event-LLM pattern. Unaddressed second-order issue: the butlers fleet itself generates heavy GitHub activity under owner credentials (~115 commits in 2 days per this pursuit's own framing), so any GitHub signal needs a repo allowlist/exclusion to avoid the system observing its own agents as 'owner workday'.
findings.detail: The roadmap's 'GitHub is not a connector at all' framing (§7.1) correctly rejects notification fan-out but wrongly concludes email metadata is the only GitHub substrate. An hourly ETag poll emitting one daily aggregate is S-cost and strictly better occupation-adapter evidence.

findings.title: ActivityWatch connector is structurally single-device: first-match bucket selection silently drops additional devices, and the connector shipped with no openspec capability spec
findings.evidence: src/butlers/connectors/activitywatch.py:375-380 — find_bucket_id() returns 'the first bucket id whose type field matches', so if a second device (work laptop via bu-pr47l, or a phone running aw-android syncing via aw-sync) pushes its buckets to the same AW server, its currentwindow/afkstatus buckets are silently ignored rather than merged or surfaced. Roadmap candidate 2 (§4.3) frames multi-machine as 'deployment/config, not code' — this line shows it is also code. Separately, openspec/specs/ contains connector-* specs for every other shipped connector (gmail, spotify, steam, owntracks, home-assistant, etc.) but no connector-activitywatch spec exists (verified against the 180-entry spec list), so the connector candidate 2 proposes to extend has no normative contract to extend.
findings.detail: Phone attention is plausibly the single largest uncaptured attention sink for the chronicler's occupation adapter, and aw-android exists in the ActivityWatch ecosystem; the roadmap's candidate 2 scoped 'multi-machine' to the work laptop only and never mentions the phone.

findings.title: Lifestyle consumption (shows, books, films) is a fifth under-sensed domain the roadmap's coverage analysis omitted despite an explicit manifesto promise
findings.evidence: roster/lifestyle/MANIFESTO.md promises 'Track what you're consuming: the show you just started, the book you're reading, the game you've been playing' — but roster/lifestyle/butler.toml enables only [modules.spotify] and [modules.steam] (lines 66-68): music and games are sensed, watching/reading are freeform-text-only, the exact capture shape the roadmap diagnosed for food ('logged only if the owner types a freeform message', §6.1) and fixed with /meal. The roadmap's domain skew analysis (§1: 'money, attention, food, and work are under-sensed') stopped at the ingestion-audit's four domains and never re-checked manifesto promises for other starving butlers. RFC 0018's media catalogue assessed only YouTube and podcasts (0018:154-158) — local media servers (Jellyfin/Plex webhooks: keyless, local, zero egress, HA-adjacent doctrine profile) and a /watched quick-log were never evaluated.

findings.title: RFC 0018's FileWatch-base deferral rationale goes stale the moment roadmap candidate 1 ships — the sequencing unlock is unrecorded
findings.evidence: RFC 0018:190-192 defers the FileWatch base because 'No v1 connector watches the filesystem, so the base has no current consumer and is not built' — and gates Obsidian (0018:121), Apple Health export (0018:109), and Kindle clippings on it. Roadmap candidate 1 builds exactly that consumer (a 'watched-directory trigger', §3.3: 'grep confirms no drop_folder / watch-folder anywhere today'). Neither document notes that shipping candidate 1 dissolves the no-consumer objection and re-prices the whole drop-folder class of deferred connectors from M-with-prerequisite to S; RFC 0018's own doctrine ('extract the abstraction only once multiple in-scope connectors demand it', 0018:205-206) then actively demands the extraction when the second drop-folder appears.

audits.jarvis_gap: The 07-10 connector roadmap (bu-dyq22) is a genuinely strong supply-side document — its four candidates are correctly scoped as extensions rather than greenfield, and its deferral calls (SGFinDex, Slack, aggregators) are doctrine-sound. Its residual gap is methodological: it derived under-sensed domains from the ingestion audit's volume skew, not from the manifestos, so it never asked 'which butler is currently promising something its capture substrate cannot deliver.' That lens exposes what the roadmap missed: travel promises pre-announcement delay/gate alerts with literally zero flight-status capture (a binding-manifesto violation under vision.md rule 6), and lifestyle promises consumption tracking while sensing only music and games. Within the four candidates, three are under-specified in ways that matter: candidate 1 designs a permanent monthly manual ritual into finance when the Gmail attachment pipeline already captures bank e-statement PDFs as unfetched attachment_refs rows (the JARVIS bar is 'the ledger is simply true,' not 'the owner remembers to download PDFs'); candidate 4a's email-metadata digest measures inbound noise rather than owner output because GitHub self-activity never generates notification email; and candidate 2's 'multi-machine is just deployment' claim is contradicted by find_bucket_id()'s first-match bucket selection, which structurally drops every device after the first — while the phone, the largest attention sink, is absent from the plan entirely. Finally, the roadmap and RFC 0018 fail to record their own sequencing synergy: candidate 1's watched-folder trigger is the first FileWatch consumer, which re-prices the entire deferred drop-folder class (Obsidian, Kindle, app exports) to S.
audits.ideal: Perception coverage is driven by manifesto promises, not volume skew: every butler's binding promises are periodically audited against its capture substrate, and a promise without a feed is treated as a doctrine defect with two exits — build the bounded feed or amend the manifesto. Concretely: finance runs on a zero-touch ledger where bank e-statements auto-flow from Gmail attachments through local PDF→CSV extraction into the dedup'd transaction spine, with the drop-folder as fallback; the chronicler's workday is corroborated by owner-authored GitHub events (fleet repos excluded) plus multi-device ActivityWatch spanning desktop, work laptop, and phone; travel either polls flight status inside trip windows (cost bounded by travel.legs) or honestly promises only what Gmail gives it; lifestyle senses watching/reading through a local media-server feed or a /watched quick-log, mirroring /meal. All new capture stays inside the existing doctrine profile — local-first, no per-event LLM, no standing third-party credential unless the value clearly exceeds the trust cost — and every shipped connector has a normative connector-* openspec contract (activitywatch's is missing today). RFC 0018 stays the living deferral ledger, amended when a prerequisite (FileWatch base) quietly becomes real.

moves.title: Bank e-statement auto-capture: Gmail attachment triage → finance import pipeline (supersedes candidate 1's manual-first framing)
moves.why: Bank statement PDFs already land in switchboard.attachment_refs as lazy metadata on every statement email; wiring a deterministic bank-sender triage rule to eager-fetch and feed candidate 1's PDF→CSV extractor makes the finance ledger zero-touch instead of a monthly download ritual. Zero new egress, zero new credentials — strictly dominates the drop-folder as the primary path. Serves the finance manifesto ('authoritative ledger').
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/connectors/gmail.py (ATTACHMENT_POLICY, _process_attachments); switchboard.attachment_refs + BlobStore on-demand fetch (docs/connectors/attachment-handling.md); new deterministic triage rule (bank-sender allowlist + application/pdf → eager fetch + route_to: finance) in the pre-classification triage layer (docs/architecture/pre-classification-triage.md), owner-confirmed per RFC 0021; candidate 1's local PDF→CSV extractor; POST /api/finance/transactions/bulk with composite dedup (openspec/specs/bulk-transaction-ingestion/spec.md). Spec deltas: connector-gmail, ingestion-policy, bulk-transaction-ingestion.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Bank-sender allowlist + .ics-style deterministic triage rule with eager PDF fetch; 2) route fetched statement blobs into the candidate-1 extractor → bulk import; 3) demote drop-folder to fallback in the roadmap doc; 4) import-status surface note (import_batches was dropped in finance migration 007 — status UI is new work either way).

moves.title: GitHub owner-activity events connector feeding the work digest (corrects candidate 4a's email-only premise)
moves.why: GitHub never emails you your own pushes/PRs/reviews, so candidate 4a's email_metadata_refs digest measures inbound noise, not owner output. A free, ETag-conditional hourly poll of GET /users/{login}/events yields the strongest deterministic workday corroborator for the chronicler occupation adapter at S cost, emitting only a nightly aggregate (RFC 0014 §D5 compliant — never per-event fanout). Serves the chronicler manifesto (retrospective workday truth).
moves.integration_points: New src/butlers/connectors/github_events.py (cursor_store checkpoint = last event id + ETag; heartbeat per connector-base-spec); Tier 1 PAT in butler_secrets via the account-registry pattern; MANDATORY repo/org exclusion list so butlers-fleet activity under owner credentials is not counted as owner workday; emits into the same work_digest chronicler adapter candidate 4a builds (alongside, not instead of, the email-metadata digest). Spec: new openspec/specs/connector-github-events + chronicler-source-compatibility delta.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Poller + checkpoint + fleet-repo exclusion; 2) nightly deterministic aggregate (PRs authored, repos touched, active-hours span); 3) join with 4a's email digest in one work_digest episode; 4) one bounded narration call/day shared with 4a.

moves.title: Trip-window flight-status capture — or a travel manifesto amendment (owner decision)
moves.why: The travel manifesto's promise of pre-announcement delay/gate alerts is binding under vision.md rule 6 and currently backed by nothing. Polling a status API only inside T-48h..arrival windows derived from travel.legs bounds a paid API (AeroAPI-class, ~$1/query) to dozens of calls per trip — affordable and doctrine-clean because it is trip-gated, not standing. If the owner declines the spend, the honest alternative is amending MANIFESTO.md to promise only Gmail-derived change detection.
moves.integration_points: roster/travel/butler.toml cron (activates only when travel.legs has type='flight' with departure_at in window); new flight_status module tool in roster/travel/tools/ (module, not connector — the trigger is the butler's own schedule + its own trip data, per the adding-connectors decision tree); status writes to travel.legs.metadata JSONB (no migration needed); alerts via core-notify boundary; Tier 1 API key in butler_secrets. Spec delta: butler-travel. Alternative slice: manifesto amendment PR (S) + RFC 0018 note.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Owner-decision bead: paid status API vs manifesto amendment; 2a) if build: window-gated poller tool + leg-status writeback + delay/gate notify; 2b) if amend: rewrite the two over-promising manifesto clauses; 3) either way, record in RFC 0018 that travel real-time was decided, not forgotten.

moves.title: Multi-device ActivityWatch: fix first-match bucket selection + aw-android phone coverage (extends candidate 2)
moves.why: find_bucket_id() takes the first bucket per type, structurally dropping every additional device even when aw-sync lands them on the same server — so candidate 2's 'multi-machine is deployment, not code' is wrong, and the phone (largest attention sink) is missing from the plan entirely. Per-device attention is the difference between 'desktop idle, owner absent' and 'owner on phone for 2h'. Serves the chronicler occupation/attention surface.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/connectors/activitywatch.py:375-380 — iterate ALL buckets per type, keyed by the hostname suffix in the bucket id; add device/host label to connectors.activitywatch_events rows and to src/butlers/chronicler/adapters/activitywatch.py episode provenance; aw-android + aw-sync deployment to the polled AW server (config, once the code merges devices). Also file the missing openspec/specs/connector-activitywatch spec — the connector currently has no normative contract to extend.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Multi-bucket iteration + device label (code); 2) connector-activitywatch openspec capability spec (governance debt from bu-whhll.6); 3) aw-android rollout + phone-vs-desktop split in the chronicler day surface; 4) fold into candidate 2's category-only privacy toggle.

moves.title: Lifestyle consumption capture: local media-server watch feed with /watched quick-log fallback
moves.why: The lifestyle manifesto promises tracking 'the show you just started, the book you're reading' but only music (Spotify) and games (Steam) are sensed — the identical freeform-text-only gap the roadmap fixed for food with /meal. A Jellyfin/Plex feed is keyless, local, zero-egress (the same doctrine profile that made HA/OwnTracks/ActivityWatch acceptable); if the owner runs no media server, the /watched//reading telegram quick-log costs S and mirrors the /meal pattern exactly. Serves the lifestyle manifesto and the chronicler's evening episodes.
moves.integration_points: First: check whether a media server is registered in Home Assistant (HA subsumption per RFC 0018 doctrine — an HA media_player entity feed may need zero new connector, only a home_assistant_filter significance rule + chronicler adapter). Else: new local webhook/poll connector (Jellyfin has native webhooks) → new lifestyle consumption table (module migration under roster/lifestyle or src/butlers/modules/) + chronicler watching-episode adapter. Fallback: telegram /watched quick-log module tool onto the same table. Spec: butler-lifestyle delta + (if built) new connector spec.
moves.slice_plan: 1) HA-subsumption check (may collapse the whole move to a filter rule); 2) consumption table + module tools; 3) capture path (webhook connector or quick-log); 4) weekly-digest + chronicler wiring.

moves.title: RFC 0018 amendment: record the FileWatch-base unlock and re-price the drop-folder class
moves.why: Candidate 1's watched-directory trigger is the first filesystem-watching consumer, which invalidates RFC 0018's stated reason for deferring the FileWatch base and silently re-prices Obsidian, Kindle clippings, and app-export (MyFitnessPal/Apple-Health-style) drop-folders from M-with-prerequisite to S. Leaving the rationale stale invites either premature re-litigation or missed cheap wins — the RFC exists precisely so 'the same debates need not be relitigated'. Pure governance, no code.
moves.integration_points: about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0018-connector-scope-and-deferral-rationale.md (Deferred Infrastructure Bases section, :186-206) — amendment note conditioned on candidate 1 shipping; docs/plans/2026-07-10-connector-roadmap-proposal.md gains a sequencing note; extraction rule stays intact (build the shared base only when the SECOND drop-folder consumer is approved, per 0018:205-206).
moves.slice_plan: One doc PR after the candidate-1 epic merges: amend RFC 0018 + cross-link the roadmap; list the three re-priced candidates without scheduling any of them.

findings.title: Revoked Codex OAuth token kills top-priority tiers and the failover classifier default-closes it — routed messages and crons die with verified same-tier alternatives one slot away
findings.evidence: Live session b03d3af4-02b4-40f4-a524-9ed71809da72 (health, trigger=route, google_health sleep event): error 'RuntimeError: Codex CLI exited with code 1: Your access token could not be refreshed because your refresh token was revoked. Please log out and sign in again.', duration 3999ms, success=false, zero tokens. public.model_dispatch_attempts last 48h: suppressed=29 (gpt-5.6-luna 20, gpt-5.6-sol 8), all with reason 'unknown_runtime_error: RuntimeError did not match any failover-eligible pattern; default-closed'. Sessions API last 100: 24 gpt-5.6-luna failures + 7 gpt-5.6-sol failures; failed sessions include schedule:weekly-health-summary, schedule:remind-*, schedule:calendar-event-*, schedule:weekly-progress-digest. Mechanism: src/butlers/core/failover_classifier.py:99-116 — _PROVIDER_AUTH_MARKERS lacks any of 'refresh token', 'revoked', 'log out and sign in', and classify_failover_eligibility matches only str(exc).lower() (line ~322); process_info stderr (which contains '401 Unauthorized' and 'token_expired', both would match existing markers) is consulted only by _is_opencode_pre_tool_call_api_error (line ~517). Catalog (public.model_catalog live): gpt-5.6-luna is top-priority workhorse (36) with verified opencode-go/mimo-v2.5 (35) directly below — never attempted. gpt-5.6-sol is top reasoning (25) and top specialty (30). Every codex-runtime entry shares the same revoked ChatGPT credential.
findings.detail: One revoked refresh token silently disables the workhorse, reasoning, and specialty tiers' primaries; the classifier's default-closed contract (correct in spirit) converts a textbook pre-invocation systemic auth failure into a terminal loss of owner-visible work (health ingestion, weekly summaries, reminders, calendar events). Two independent gaps compound: marker vocabulary misses the Codex revoked-refresh-token phrasing, and stderr — where unambiguous markers exist — is never consulted.

findings.title: No dispatch-outcome feedback into the model catalog: a 100%-failing model keeps last_verified_ok=true and top priority indefinitely
findings.evidence: public.model_catalog live: gpt-5.6-luna last_verified_ok=t, enabled=t, priority 36 (workhorse) despite 20+ consecutive auth failures over hours (model_dispatch_attempts). last_verified_ok is written only by POST /api/settings/models/verify-all — a manual, 60s-rate-limited endpoint (src/butlers/api/routers/model_settings.py:613-636, _verify_all_last_run sentinel at line 47-49); grep confirms no other writer in src/. model_routing._RESOLVE_SQL (model_routing.py:294-295) filters only on 'last_verified_ok IS DISTINCT FROM false', so every new dispatch re-elects the dead model, pays ~4s of subprocess+auth-retry latency, and terminally fails.
findings.detail: The dispatch loop already writes rich per-attempt provenance (model_dispatch_attempts, dispatch_failures) but nothing reads it back into selection. Failure never demotes; only a human clicking verify-all does. This is 'failure impersonating health' at the routing layer: the Models tab shows a green verified badge on a model that has not completed a session in hours.

findings.title: Switchboard classification SLA broken 28x at p99: median 20.8s, p99 139.2s vs manifesto '<5s p99', at ~29K input tokens per classification
findings.evidence: switchboard.sessions, 259 successful classification sessions last 7d: median duration 20,776ms, p99 139,217ms, avg input_tokens 29,471. roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md SLA table: 'Message classification latency | < 5 s p99 under normal load'. Ledger: purpose=classification = 259 calls / 22.2M input tokens per week; purpose=route = 387 calls / 59.3M input tokens — together ~80% of all weekly input tokens (~102M). A health route session (the second hop of every event) has median 25.8s (health.sessions, 156 rows/7d), so message→action latency is ~47s median through the double hop.
findings.detail: Reported as measurement, not a re-filed remedy: the API-direct classification lane re-enable is a known pending owner decision and the classification fast-lane spec move is known-deferred. This gives that decision its missing quantitative urgency — every inbound event pays a full CLI subprocess + MCP handshake + 29K-token prompt to emit ~28 output tokens of routing decision, 4-28x outside the staffer's own binding contract.

findings.title: Static fallback model is a Claude model paired with the Codex runtime — policy-contradicting and non-functional by construction
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:145 _FALLBACK_MODEL_ID = 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'; DEFAULT_RUNTIME_TYPE = 'codex' (src/butlers/core/runtimes/base.py:18). In the catalog-degraded path (spawner.py:967-972) the spawner dispatches model=claude-haiku-4-5 on the codex adapter — a ChatGPT-backend CLI that cannot serve an Anthropic model id. All claude-* catalog entries are enabled=false live (owner policy: no claude-*/api-haiku routing for butlers; opencode-go mimo-v2.5 is the cheap primary). Queue-rejection SpawnerResults also stamp model=_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID (spawner.py:637, 656) though nothing ran.
findings.detail: The 'deterministic last-resort' the comment promises is neither policy-conformant nor runnable: catalog outage would produce codex exec --model claude-haiku-... failures, i.e. the degraded path is a second outage. Fallback should be the owner's cost-independent primary (opencode-go/mimo-v2.5 on opencode) or an explicit fail-fast.

findings.title: Schedule-task spend is unbounded in practice: per-task token budgets shipped (core_050) but only one butler uses them; upcoming-travel-check burns ~860K input tokens per run
findings.evidence: public.token_usage_ledger 7d: schedule:upcoming-travel-check = 6 runs / 5,160,357 input tokens (~860K/run) vs schedule:eod-tomorrow-prep ~155K/run. Enforcement path exists end-to-end: scheduler reads max_token_budget per entry (src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:596-611, column added core_050) and the spawner enforces it as a guardrail (spawner.py trigger param max_token_budget → _check_token_budget). grep across roster/*/butler.toml: only roster/relationship/butler.toml sets max_token_budget (lines 31, 45); zero schedule entries declare complexity except two in chronicler (butler.toml:148,211), so nearly every cron dispatches at workhorse default.
findings.detail: Distinct from the parked 'deterministic precondition gates' idea (which skips spawns): the bounding mechanism is already built and tested, it is simply unadopted as a roster convention, and cron complexity tiering (cheap for digest/reminder-shaped tasks) is likewise available but unused.

audits.ideal: The trigger→spawn→act loop behaves like a reflex arc with a budget-conscious brainstem. Model selection is a closed loop: every dispatch outcome (success, auth failure, rate limit, timeout) feeds back into catalog eligibility within seconds — a tripped breaker demotes a dying model before the second owner-visible message is lost, a background probe restores it when the credential is fixed, and the Models tab shows breaker state as evidence-bearing truth rather than a stale manual verification badge. Failover classification recognizes every pre-invocation systemic failure a real provider actually emits — matched against both the exception and the adapter's stderr — so a dead primary costs one 4-second probe, not a lost health reading. Classification meets its own manifesto SLA (<5s p99) because zero-reasoning routing work never pays for a CLI subprocess and a 29K-token prompt; the full-session lane is reserved for work that needs judgment. Non-interactive telemetry coalesces at the route boundary so a night of sleep/steps/heart-rate events costs one butler session, not five. Every scheduled task declares its complexity tier and token budget in the roster as identity, and the degraded-path fallback is the owner's own cost-independent primary — nothing in the loop can silently route spend to a provider the owner has excluded.
audits.jarvis_gap: The loop's economics are inverted from JARVIS: ~80% of all weekly input tokens (81.5M of ~102M) are spent on the plumbing hops — classification (22.2M, median 20.8s, 28x outside the switchboard's own <5s p99 SLA) and route dispatch (59.3M at ~153K tokens and ~26s median per event) — before any domain reasoning happens, giving a ~47s median message→action latency where JARVIS implies near-instant acknowledgment. Worse, the selection layer is open-loop: a single revoked Codex OAuth token currently kills the top-priority workhorse/reasoning/specialty models, the failover classifier default-closes the unrecognized error text (29 suppressed failovers in 48h) so verified same-tier alternatives one priority-slot away are never tried, and last_verified_ok — writable only by a manual dashboard click — keeps advertising the dead models as healthy. Health telemetry, weekly summaries, reminders, and calendar crons died over hours with the fleet dashboard showing green model badges: failure impersonating health at the exact layer whose job is picking something that works. Capability-wise the loop has the right primitives (per-attempt provenance, same-tier failover, per-task budgets, tier declarations, prompt-cache-stable composition at 55-66% hit rates) but they are unwired into each other: provenance is written and never read back, budgets exist and are set by one butler, tiers exist and crons all default to workhorse.

moves.title: Complete the auth-failure vocabulary and give the failover classifier a stderr channel
moves.why: The live outage's root mechanism: 'refresh token was revoked / log out and sign in again' matches no _PROVIDER_AUTH_MARKERS entry, and the stderr that contains unambiguous markers ('401 Unauthorized', 'token_expired') is never consulted. 28 failovers suppressed in 48h with verified same-tier candidates available; every one was a lost owner-visible action. This is the single highest leverage-per-line fix in the loop.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/failover_classifier.py — extend _PROVIDER_AUTH_MARKERS (refresh token, revoked, sign in again, refresh_token_invalidated) and add a bounded stderr-matching gate (FailoverContext.process_info['stderr'], only when tool_calls is empty, keeping the default-closed side-effect contract); tests/core/test_failover_classifier.py marker-bucket disjointness tests; no schema change. Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract (routing execution/buffer durability) and every domain butler manifesto's message-handling promise.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add markers + regression test built from the exact live error string; 2) add opt-in stderr matching for pre-tool-call failures with disjointness tests; 3) backfill a QA canary that replays the revoked-token stderr through the classifier.

moves.title: Dispatch-outcome circuit breaker on model_catalog entries
moves.why: The catalog re-elects a 100%-failing model indefinitely because nothing reads dispatch provenance back into selection; last_verified_ok is manual-only. A rolling breaker (N consecutive pre-work systemic failures opens; cooldown + half-open probe closes) turns hours of silent loss into one probe's worth of latency, and makes the Models tab tell the truth.
moves.integration_points: New public.model_breaker_state (or breaker columns on model_catalog) written by the spawner failover loop (it already writes model_dispatch_attempts at spawner.py:315-363); eligibility clause in model_routing._RESOLVE_SQL and _NEXT_SAME_TIER_SQL alongside 'last_verified_ok IS DISTINCT FROM false'; half-open probe reuses the verify-all single-model verification internals (model_settings.py); Models tab shows tripped/cooldown/half-open state with the triggering error evidence; alembic core migration. Serves vision.md's earned-calm bar (failure never impersonates health) and the five-second-fleet-verification north star; amend openspec model-catalog spec §3.2 routing contract.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Breaker state table + spawner writes on runtime_failure/suppressed with systemic reasons; 2) resolver exclusion + half-open probe cron; 3) Models tab breaker chip + attention-ledger push on breaker open.

moves.title: Automated hourly model verification sweep
moves.why: verify-all exists but fires only on a dashboard click, so a revoked credential stays 'verified' until a human notices downstream breakage. Running the same 1-token verification hourly for enabled entries bounds the staleness of last_verified_ok to one hour, complementing the breaker (breaker = fast per-dispatch reaction; sweep = background truth that also RESTORES entries when the credential is fixed).
moves.integration_points: Refactor verify-all internals (src/butlers/api/routers/model_settings.py:613+) into a callable shared with a scheduled task; host it on the QA staffer's schedule (roster/qa/butler.toml) or a core daemon cron — deterministic infra work, no LLM session needed; audit.append('models.verify_all') per run already exists; surfaces via existing last_verified_at/latency columns. Serves the QA staffer's infrastructure-verification contract; small delta to openspec model-catalog spec.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Extract callable + wire hourly cron with jitter and per-entry cost guard (1-token probes); 2) QA discovery source consumes consecutive-failure streaks to file an investigation naming the credential.

moves.title: Telemetry-event coalescing at the route boundary
moves.why: Route dispatch is the single largest spend line (59.3M input tokens/week, ~153K tokens and ~26s median per event) and non-interactive telemetry (google_health sleep/steps, home, location; addressed=false) arrives in bursts that each pay a full butler session. Micro-batching per (target butler, channel) with a 60-120s debounce dispatches ONE session carrying N events — cutting route sessions 30-50% on telemetry-heavy days with zero owner-perceptible latency cost (this class of event has no interactive reply).
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py routing-execution path (gate on addressed=false + non-interactive channel + policy_tier=default); switchboard-schema ingestion buffer for the debounce window; route prompt envelope becomes a list of INPUT CONTEXT blocks; sessions↔ingestion provenance needs a many-to-one join (new session_ingestion_events table replacing the single ingestion_event_id FK for batched dispatches); degraded/replay semantics per connector-replay-queue spec. Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract — requires a manifesto amendment clause ('routing execution may batch non-interactive telemetry per target butler'); domain butlers unaffected (they already receive structured requests).

findings.title: Autonomy promotion is mathematically unreachable — exact-args fingerprinting fragments every action class below the threshold
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/approvals/autonomy_tracker.py:35-56 (compute_fingerprint hashes canonical JSON of tool_name + FULL tool_args) and :122-151 (check_promotion_threshold, default 5). Live DB (butlers-db-dev, read-only): 95 manual approvals across home/messenger/relationship spread over 53 distinct fingerprints; the single highest fingerprint count is 4 (relationship_assert_fact) — below the threshold of 5; relationship.autonomy_suggestions = 0 rows, approval_rules = 0 rows across all three approvals-enabled schemas. relationship_assert_fact alone has 33 approvals fragmented into 24 fingerprints; telegram_send_message 10 approvals into 5 fingerprints. Any arg that varies (message text, entity ids, dates) makes accumulation impossible, so in the system's entire operating history not one promotion suggestion has ever been minted.
findings.detail: The ONLY machine that converts owner trust into widened autonomy is keyed so narrowly it structurally never fires for arg-bearing tools. This is distinct from bu-4pq0s (owner disposition on the ingestion skip/metadata_only rule tier) — that gate is about switchboard ingestion rules, not the approvals autonomy fingerprint ratchet. Vision.md's core success criterion ('the owner trusts it with progressively more autonomy') has no working substrate.

findings.title: The rule-maturity ladder is a dead organ: 2 candidate rules fleet-wide, zero structural consumers, its outcome table already deleted as write-orphaned
findings.evidence: Live /api/memory/stats: total_rules=2, candidate=2, established=0, proven=0, anti_pattern=0 across 9 memory-enabled butlers. src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/006_drop_rule_applications.py:1-19 records that rule_applications was INSERT-only with no reader and was dropped as cruft. Grep across src/butlers outside modules/memory finds no behavioral consumer of maturity — rules only reach sessions as soft prompt text via memory_context '## Active Rules' (tools/context.py) and the dashboard (api/routers/memory.py). Nothing maps 'proven' to any permission, gate, or approval scope.
findings.detail: Combined with the fingerprint finding: memory has a trust ladder with no rungs used and approvals has rungs no one can climb — two disconnected trust machines, neither of which lets the graph earn autonomous action. Rule scarcity itself is downstream of consolidation being gated (bu-4qfhl, known — not re-filed here); the missing consumer is the NEW gap: even a decided bu-4qfhl produces rules that go nowhere. Note docs/modules/memory.md:148 still documents the dropped rule_applications table.

findings.title: Decay has no reinforcement input: usage signal is recorded on every recall but the confidence formula ignores it; memory_confirm used on 21 of 4,017 facts ever
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:400-425 — effective_confidence(confidence, decay_rate, last_confirmed_at) keys ONLY on last_confirmed_at. Yet search.py:549-550 bumps reference_count and last_referenced_at on every recall hit (feeding only the display recency score), and storage.py:1887-1912 maintains the same counters on memory_get. Live DB: facts where last_confirmed_at ever moved past created_at = 1+7+4+0+6+3+0+0+0 = 21 across all nine schemas (4,017 facts). fading_facts=0 today only because the sweep isn't live yet.
findings.detail: When bu-5ud8p's decay sweep activates (in-flight; it writes validity='fading' + backfill — it does NOT change the input signal), every fact trends monotonically toward fading regardless of daily use: a fact the fleet recalls 500 times decays identically to one never touched. The counterweight data already exists on the row; nothing consumes it. This is a lifecycle-mechanics gap, distinct from the known-deferred 'confidence calibration' (making values match reality) and 'staleness SLAs' items.

findings.title: Cross-butler full-content reads are effectively nonexistent: delegation ledger has ZERO rows since ship, and the catalog is summaries-only with no dereference or traversal
findings.evidence: Live DB: SELECT count(*) FROM public.delegation_ledger → 0, eight days after delegate_ask/receive/answer shipped fleet-wide (src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py, core_162). openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md §'Public memory discovery catalog table': catalog 'is a discovery index, NOT a canonical store' — full retrieval requires the owning schema, which butlers cannot read (vision.md rule 3). entity_neighbors traversal is schema-local only (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:657-760, recursive CTE over the local facts table); public.memory_catalog carries object_entity_id on 101 rows that no code traverses. No mention of delegate_ask in any roster/*/CLAUDE.md.
findings.detail: The only path from a Fleet Knowledge summary to full canonical content is delegate_ask — an async LLM spawn in the target butler — and it has never been invoked once. So in practice cross-butler knowledge = 10%-of-budget catalog summaries (spawner.py:1370 injects with include_fleet_knowledge=True) and nothing else. Distinct from the known-deferred 'delegation-ledger consumer' (a dashboard READ surface); this is producer-side adoption plus a missing deterministic dereference.

findings.title: The knowledge graph is a star, not a graph: 3.4% of facts carry an object edge, and home anchoring is at 17%
findings.evidence: Live DB per-schema query on {schema}.facts: object_entity_id set on 137/4,024 facts fleet-wide (relationship 57, lifestyle 37, general 25, finance 11, health 4, switchboard 3, home/education/travel 0). entity_id anchoring: home 50/302 (17%) vs 91-100% everywhere else. public.entities = 828 entities; catalog rows with entity_id 3,633/3,973.
findings.detail: Distinct from the closed bu-xgz7g epic, which fed relationship's Store-A entity_facts edges from calendar signal; the memory-side (Store-B-style) graphs of the OTHER eight butlers never got an equivalent pass, so entity_neighbors has almost no paths to walk outside relationship, and any future cross-butler traversal starts from a near-empty edge set. Home is also the worst-anchored schema, meaning its 302 facts largely can't join the graph at all.

audits.ideal: The graph is a trust engine, not an archive. Every fact carries provenance, an entity anchor, and — when it names a second party — a traversable edge; the fleet's nine memory schemas plus the catalog form one navigable knowledge plane where a butler can walk from a summary hit to the full canonical fact deterministically (narrow RFC-0010 grant), reserving LLM-to-LLM delegation for questions that need reasoning, not lookups. Lifecycle is a closed loop with both directions live: consolidation promotes episodes into facts and rules; decay fades what the fleet stops touching; recall usage, re-assertion, and owner engagement automatically re-confirm what the household actually lives on. Above the fact layer sits a single earned-autonomy ledger: behavioral rules mature through evidenced applications, approvals accumulate over action *classes* (scope templates, not exact-arg hashes), and when the two agree, the system mints an owner-confirmable autonomy grant whose dossier doors open onto the exact approvals and rule applications that earned it — and whose revocation is automatic when harm evidence arrives. The owner watches autonomy be earned in five seconds on one panel, and vision.md's 'progressively more autonomy' is a mechanism, not a hope.
audits.jarvis_gap: The graph GROWS fine — 4,017 facts, 91%+ entity anchoring in most schemas, a populated cross-butler catalog (3,973 rows) injected into every spawn, and catalog-routed delegation shipped — but trust never COMPOUNDS. Promotion is gated (consolidation has never run — known, bu-4qfhl), decay is about to become one-way (usage signal recorded on every recall but ignored by the confidence formula; 21 manual confirms ever), the rule-maturity ladder has 2 candidate rules and zero structural consumers, and the approvals autonomy ratchet hashes exact args so 95 real approvals produced zero promotion suggestions in the system's entire history. Cross-butler reads stop at summaries: the only full-content path (delegate_ask) has literally never been used, and no deterministic dereference or cross-schema traversal exists despite the catalog carrying the provenance pointers and edge columns for both. Net: every individual organ of a self-trusting knowledge graph exists — provenance columns, maturity states, fingerprints, catalog pointers, reference counters — but no vessel connects them, so the graph can grow forever without ever earning the system a single unit of autonomy.

moves.title: Earned-autonomy bridge: one trust ledger from graph to gates (scope-template fingerprints + rule-maturity crosswalk)
moves.why: The vision's core success criterion — progressively more autonomy — currently has no working mechanism: exact-args fingerprints never accumulate (95 approvals, 53 fingerprints, max 4 < threshold 5, zero suggestions ever) and rule maturity has no consumer. Fix both by joining them: per-tool scope templates declare which args are identity-bearing (chat_id yes, text no) so approvals accumulate over action classes; a 'proven' memory rule whose scope maps to a gated tool mints an owner-confirmed promotion suggestion whose dossier doors open onto the exact approvals/applications that earned it; auto-approved executions write outcome evidence back to the rule so anti_pattern demotion auto-mints a revocation suggestion. Honors the bu-4pq0s owner-confirmed disposition (that gate covers only the ingestion skip/metadata_only tier — this is the approvals ratchet).
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/modules/approvals/autonomy_tracker.py:35-56 (compute_fingerprint → scope-template fingerprint), autonomy_suggestions.py (evidence-bearing dossier), modules/memory/storage.py rule maturity transitions (promotion hook), a small rule↔approval-scope mapping table in each approvals-enabled schema (home/messenger/relationship), openspec deltas to module-memory + a new module-approvals autonomy requirement, /api/approvals suggestions surface + Trust Console panel. Serves vision.md §What Success Looks Like; messenger + relationship manifestos (the approvals-enabled butlers).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Scope-template fingerprint (per-tool stable-arg declaration + migration re-keying history) — suggestions start firing on existing data. 2) Evidence-door dossier on promotion suggestions. 3) Rule-maturity → suggestion crosswalk + outcome writeback/revocation. 4) Trust Console 'earned autonomy' panel.

moves.title: Reinforcement-aware lifecycle: recall usage and re-assertion feed the decay clock
moves.why: Decay is about to go one-way: bu-5ud8p's sweep will fade facts by last_confirmed_at alone, but the counterweight signal already exists unread on every row — reference_count/last_referenced_at are bumped on every recall (search.py:549) and memory_confirm is used on 21/4,017 facts ever. Add a bounded usage term (or rate-limited soft-confirm on recall) to effective_confidence, and make idempotent re-assertion of an existing fact a confirmation event instead of a silent no-op. The facts the household actually lives on stay hot; the rest fade honestly. Extends bu-5ud8p (which owns the sweep/vocabulary, not the input signal) and is distinct from deferred 'confidence calibration'.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:400-425 (effective_confidence signature gains last_referenced_at/reference_count), search.py:518-551 (recall bump → rate-limited soft-confirm writing memory_events audit rows), storage.py:1306-1312 (idempotency-hit path → confirm_memory at :2197), storage.py decay sweep queries (:2576, :2637), openspec module-memory spec delta on the decay requirement. Serves general's manifesto ('your collection grows richer over time') and every memory-enabled butler.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Fold usage into effective_confidence behind a config weight + tests. 2) Re-assertion-confirms on the idempotency path. 3) Memory page shows 'kept alive by use' vs 'manually confirmed' provenance on the validity chip.

moves.title: Deterministic cross-butler dereference + catalog-edge traversal (stop spawning an LLM to read a row)
moves.why: Today a Fleet Knowledge hit dead-ends at a summary: full content requires delegate_ask (an async LLM spawn in the target butler, used 0 times ever) because butlers can't read each other's schemas. Add memory_catalog_get(source_schema, source_id) — a narrowly-granted SECURITY DEFINER dereference honoring the caller's sensitivity ceiling, documented as an RFC-0010 exception exactly like the catalog's existing narrow INSERT/UPDATE grants — plus a cross-butler mode of entity_neighbors that unions public.memory_catalog object_entity_id edges (101 rows today, untraversed by anything). Zero-reasoning lookups become deterministic; delegate_ask is reserved for questions needing the other butler's judgment.
moves.integration_points: New core migration (SECURITY DEFINER function + grant on public.memory_catalog dereference), openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog spec delta ('Cross-butler search via catalog' requirement gains a dereference clause), src/butlers/core/memory_hooks.py + modules/memory/tools/reading.py (new tool), tools/entities.py:657-760 (cross-schema traversal mode), tools/context.py Fleet Knowledge compiler (summaries link their dereference), new RFC in about/legends-and-lore/. Serves vision.md rule 3's documented-exception path and switchboard's shared-situational-awareness charter.
moves.slice_plan: 1) RFC + dereference function/tool with sensitivity ceiling tests. 2) Fleet Knowledge section emits dereferenceable pointers. 3) Cross-butler entity_neighbors over catalog edges.

moves.title: Fleet edge growth + anchoring floor: generalize edge derivation beyond relationship, gauge density per schema
moves.why: The graph is a star: 3.4% of facts fleet-wide carry object_entity_id, home/education/travel have zero edges, and home is only 17% entity-anchored — so entity_neighbors (and any future traversal) has nothing to walk outside relationship. bu-xgz7g solved this for relationship's Store-A entity_facts only. Generalize the pattern: store-time resolve-or-warn when an is_edge predicate arrives without an object entity, a per-schema scheduled derivation pass (health provider→clinic, finance merchant→org, home device→room) with an auditable src, and a per-butler anchoring%/edge% gauge on the memory page so density regressions are visible in five seconds.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/writing.py memory_store_fact (predicate_registry.is_edge validation nudge), a module-default scheduled job in modules/memory/__init__.py (mirroring memory_catalog_backfill at :79-89), predicate_registry per schema, /api/memory stats + frontend memory page gauge tile (pattern-matches bu-5ud8p's drift gauge without touching its catalog scope), openspec module-memory delta. Serves home + relationship manifestos; home also gets the anchoring backfill it needs (50/302).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Density gauge (read-only, immediate visibility). 2) Store-time is_edge resolution nudge. 3) Per-schema derivation job behind per-butler config, home first.

moves.title: delegate_ask heartbeat: advertise the tool where the need appears and canary it weekly
moves.why: The cross-butler ask path shipped 2026-07-04 and has ZERO ledger rows — an unexercised organ rots (and its 30s route timeout, catalog-resolution quality, and answer loop have never run outside tests). Two cheap levers: (a) the Fleet Knowledge context section footer names the owning butler of each hit and says 'delegate_ask to get the full/current answer' — putting the affordance exactly where the summary runs out; (b) a weekly QA canary drives one real delegate_ask end-to-end (ask → route → target answers → ledger row asserted) so regressions surface as QA cases, not silent decay. Producer-side adoption; deliberately does NOT build the deferred dashboard delegation-ledger consumer.

Serves switchboard's routing charter and the qa staffer's infrastructure contract.

findings.title: Context bus has zero producers — 'shared situational awareness' has never carried a single signal
findings.evidence: Live: public.user_context has 0 rows total (and 0 active) in the long-lived dev DB (butlers-db-dev, queried read-only 2026-07-12 — same DB holds 1,232 insight_candidates rows, so it is not a fresh instance). Source: set_context()/clear_context() in src/butlers/context_bus.py have no call sites anywhere in src/ or roster/ (repo-wide grep matches only the module itself), and no MCP tool registers a context write path (RFC 0009 §Integration explicitly anticipates a check_context/set tool; none exists in src/butlers/core_tools/). Meanwhile THREE consumers are live-wired: (1) notify() dnd/sleeping suppression at src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py:667-691 via get_suppressing_context_signal (src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py:324-352, shipped bu-qvnce.8 slice 2) — this gate can structurally never fire; (2) every spawned session fetches a situational-context preamble at src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1351 → spawner_context.py:296-329 — always empty; (3) attention-ledger context reasons. about/heart-and-soul/vision.md §What Butlers Is claims the Switchboard 'maintains shared situational awareness so butlers adapt to the user's current context' — a vision-level capability that exists only as consumer plumbing. The openspec context-bus spec (openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md) specifies only the library functions and vocabulary; it contains no producer requirement, so the spec is 'satisfied' while the bus is permanently silent.
findings.detail: This is the purest 'plumbing impersonating capability' case in the collaboration fabric: RFC 0009 was accepted 2026-03-25, consumers were built and hardened across two pursuit runs, and in ~3.5 months no butler has ever asserted traveling/sleeping/meeting/dnd. Health check-ins still fire during meetings; the suppression machinery reports honest 'no signal' forever because no one can speak, not because nothing is happening.

findings.title: Cross-butler delegation loop is open at both ends: zero adoption, and answers dead-end in the ledger
findings.evidence: Live: public.delegation_ledger has 0 rows; GET /api/delegation/ledger returns {"data":[],"meta":{"total":0,...}}. Source: delegate_ask/delegate_receive/delegate_answer are registered fleet-wide (src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:55-363, non-STAFFER), but 'delegate_ask' appears NOWHERE in roster/ — no CLAUDE.md, skill, or butler.toml prompt mentions the tool, so no spawned session knows it exists or when to reach for it. The answer path terminates at record_answer (delegation_ledger row → status='answered'); delegate_ask's own docstring says 'Check back later (dashboard delegation ledger, or ask the target directly)' — no mechanism routes the answer back to the asking butler's next session, and the spec (openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md, Requirements end at 'Answering Is Asynchronous And Guarded' + 'Discoverability') has no answer-delivery requirement at all. Additionally resolve_target_via_catalog (src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py:283) searches with limit=1 — a question spanning two domains can only ever reach one butler.
findings.detail: Overlaps the known-deferred 'delegation-ledger consumer' item — reported here with NEW strengthening evidence for promotion: (a) live-confirmed zero usage since core_162 landed, (b) zero roster prompt adoption (the tool is invisible to the very LLM sessions it was built for), (c) the open loop is spec-level, not just implementation-level — v1's contract literally ends before the asker learns anything, and (d) top-1 target resolution structurally forbids multi-domain fan-out.

findings.title: Insight economy brokers a minority of voices: 4 of 9 domain butlers have scan jobs, only 3 have ever proposed
findings.evidence: Source: insight-scan scheduled jobs exist only in roster/travel/butler.toml:71, roster/health/butler.toml:45, roster/relationship/butler.toml:88, roster/finance/butler.toml:57; general, education, home, lifestyle, and chronicler butler.tomls have none (grep confirmed). Live: public.insight_candidates by origin — finance 9, health 7, relationship 1,216 (996 expired / 133 filtered / 23 delivered), travel 0 rows despite its cron. RFC 0011's motivation names candidates these butlers would own (learning streaks, device alerts, habit patterns) that today have no path to the owner.
findings.detail: Two sub-problems: participation coverage (5 domain butlers cannot compete for delivery slots at all), and travel's scan silently producing nothing (job runs, zero candidates ever — worth a QA look). The relationship butler's 996-expired pile is the deferred per-origin-scoring problem; not re-reported.

findings.title: Chronicler is excluded from the cross-butler briefing — the tomorrow-prep carries zero lived-day retrospective
findings.evidence: SPECIALIST_BUTLERS at src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:40-48 lists exactly (education, finance, health, home, lifestyle, relationship, travel); chronicler is absent, roster/chronicler/butler.toml has no daily_briefing_contribution job, and the RFC 0010 view unions only the original 7 schemas. Yet chronicler now owns the richest day-level cross-butler synthesis in the fleet (IEA day surface bu-8whey5, daily-rollup narrative bu-4qymf — both landed 07-10..07-12).
findings.detail: The EOD briefing previews tomorrow using specialist highlights but cannot say what actually happened today — the one butler whose whole manifesto is 'reconstructs lived past time from other butlers' evidence' is not in the chorus. A deterministic contribution (read chronicler's own daily rollup, write briefing/daily/<date> to chronicler.state) fits RFC 0010's guardrails exactly.

audits.jarvis_gap: The collaboration fabric is fully architected and mostly silent. The system has exactly four cross-butler channels — routing (route/notify, healthy and busy), the briefing contribution chorus (RFC 0010, working but frozen at its original 7 members), the insight broker (RFC 0011, working but carrying 3 of 9 domain voices, one of which floods it), and two channels that have never carried a single end-to-end message in their lifetimes: the situational context bus (0 rows ever in public.user_context despite three hardened consumers, including the notify dnd/sleeping gate shipped this cycle) and the delegation ledger (0 rows ever, tool invisible to every roster prompt, spec ends before the asker learns the answer). The pattern across all of it is the same: consumer-side and safety-side machinery gets built and polished (suppression gates, preambles, ledgers, dashboards, degraded flags) while the producer side — the part where a butler actually speaks to its peers — is never wired, so 'genuine collaboration' currently means each butler contributing a nightly paragraph to one briefing. Nothing in the fleet today can notice that a spending spike coincides with a trip, defer a health check-in because the calendar says you're in a meeting, or answer a question that spans two domains. JARVIS-grade collaboration is not more channels; it is making the four existing MCP-compliant channels carry real traffic, then adding the one missing primitive (a durable multi-butler plan) on top of them.
audits.ideal: Every butler both speaks and listens on the shared awareness layer: deterministic producers keep public.user_context live (calendar→meeting/focused, home→at_home, travel→traveling, health→sleeping, owner→dnd), so every spawned session opens with a true situational preamble and the already-shipped notify suppression gate actually fires — earned calm, not fabricated silence. A butler that hits the edge of its domain reaches across it in one tool call: delegate_ask fans out to every relevant peer, answers flow back into the asker's next session and (when owner-initiated) to the owner, and the whole exchange is a door on the delegation ledger. The insight broker hears all nine domain voices and runs a weekly synthesis pass that emits the correlations no single butler can see — spend×travel, sleep×meetings, nutrition×grocery — as first-class multi-provenance insights competing under the same budget. And for the goals that genuinely need a team ('plan the Tokyo trip'), a commission primitive lets the Switchboard open a durable plan, fan sub-tasks to travel/calendar/finance/health over the existing route() spine, gate owner-facing commitments through the RFC 0021 decision loop, and show the whole plan as one traceable surface. All of it MCP-only, all of it ledgered, none of it a new protocol.

moves.title: Light the context bus: deterministic producers for the five cheapest true signals
moves.why: Three consumers are already shipped and hardened (notify dnd/sleeping suppression _notifications.py:667-691, per-spawn situational preamble spawner.py:1351, attention-ledger reasons) against a table that has been empty for 3.5 months. Producers are pure infrastructure — zero LLM reasoning — so this is the highest leverage-per-token move in the whole collaboration lens: the vision's 'shared situational awareness' clause becomes true, and every domain manifesto's implicit 'right timing' promise (health check-ins, relationship prompts, finance questions) starts being kept. Serves all domain manifestos; fulfills RFC 0009 as written.
moves.integration_points: set_context()/clear_context() in src/butlers/context_bus.py (write permissions table already enforces RFC 0009's writer matrix); new deterministic jobs in src/butlers/jobs/ registered via dispatch_mode='job' butler.toml schedules (pattern: insight_scan): general→meeting/focused from the calendar module's current events, home→at_home from HA presence (extend src/butlers/jobs/home.py), travel→traveling from active trip rows, health→sleeping from an owner-declared sleep window (reuse the owner work-schedule pattern, bu-8gmzj); a small 'context' core-tool group registering set_context/check_context MCP tools so sessions can assert dnd/sick from explicit owner statements (general+switchboard per the permission table); openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md delta adding producer SHALL-requirements (the spec currently has none — that is how this stayed invisible); optional dashboard context-timeline door per RFC 0009 §Integration/RFC 0007.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: calendar→meeting/focused job on general (single writer, immediately makes preambles non-empty during workdays). Slice 2: home→at_home + travel→traveling. Slice 3: health→sleeping window (makes the shipped notify sleeping-gate live). Slice 4: set_context/check_context MCP tools for explicit dnd/sick. Slice 5: spec delta + context timeline door + attention-ledger verification that suppressed_context_bus events now occur.

moves.title: Close the delegation loop: answer return-path, fleet prompt adoption, multi-target fan-out
moves.why: delegate_ask is a complete, well-guarded, ledgered primitive that no session has ever called because no prompt mentions it, and whose answers would dead-end in a table nobody reads back. Closing the loop turns it from furniture into the fleet's inter-butler Q&A spine — the prerequisite for every cross-domain behavior (chat-widget cross-domain questions, commission sub-queries, briefing enrichment). audits.jarvis_gap: The owner's actual daily surface is Telegram, and today it is a one-way, text-only, doorless pipe. Inbound: the connector drops the content of every voice note and photo to a literal "[Voice message]"/"[Photo]" placeholder (telegram_bot.py:85-141) — the system ambiently transcribes room audio via live_listener/faster-whisper yet cannot hear a voice note the owner deliberately sends it. Outbound: delivered messages carry no door back to the trace spine (deliver.py persists session_id but the message text has no dashboard link), so "every clause a door" ends at the LAN boundary; from the phone the owner cannot verify a claim, see why something arrived, or check fleet health — five-second fleet verification is dashboard-only. Control: there is no deterministic command surface (no /status, /mute); the only phone-side lever is sending free text into LLM classification. Trust: the attention ledger — the surface built to prove silence is chosen — has no "failed" outcome, so real delivery failures (Messenger down, no recipient) are stamped "deferred" and, unlike true deferrals, are never retried; live rows confirm failure currently impersonating a benign hold. The dashboard purpose doc itself declares chat/channel surfaces primary for the owner (purpose-and-single-pane.md:11), but no spec governs that surface as a whole — openspec covers per-channel plumbing (module-telegram, core-notify, insight-delivery, time-aware-delivery) with no owner-surface contract tying tiers, doors, honesty, and style together.
audits.ideal: The phone becomes a full peer of the dashboard for the owner role, without becoming a chatbot: butlers still act on schedule, but every touchpoint is two-way, verifiable, and honest. Inbound, the owner speaks, snaps, or types — voice notes arrive as transcripts, photos as stored artifacts with vision descriptions, all through the existing Switchboard ingress (connectors normalize; butlers never know it was voice). Outbound, every delivered message ends with a compact door into the trace spine (notification → session → decision), so any claim can be verified in one tap from anywhere on the tailnet. A deterministic command lane (/status, /decisions, /spend, /mute) answers zero-reasoning reads in under a second with zero LLM spend, giving five-second fleet verification from a pocket. The attention ledger distinguishes failed from deferred, failed owner-critical pushes retry through the existing deferred flusher, and the daily briefing opens with a one-line "what I held back" recap with a door — earned calm becomes verifiable calm on the owner's primary channel. One owner-surface capability spec governs the tiers (ambient / push / digest / conversational / console), the door requirement, the hold-visibility requirement, and a shared message style vocabulary so eleven butlers speak with one voice. The dashboard stays the ops console, exactly as the purpose doc scopes it.

findings.title: Attention ledger has no 'failed' outcome — delivery failures are stamped 'deferred' and never retried

Live: GET /api/attention/ledger returns row id=ee590ef0 outcome="deferred" reason="delivery_error:ConnectionError: Failed to call tool telegram_send_message on http://localhost:41104/mcp..." with notification_ref=null — no deferred_notifications row exists, so the scheduler flush pass (src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:1589) will never deliver it.

bu-os64u.1-.4 (openspec sweep, epic-close clause, v1-status refresh, ideas ledger) and bu-1mq1d prompt unification verified landed-as-designed. Open shape defect: the decision-bead convention has zero adopters and its linter validates the empty set.

Deploy spine shipped but all five slices landed-with-gaps, and the live stack is frozen on a non-main tmp worktree with every post-07-11 04:22Z merge dark — the exact failure class the spine was built to catch, undetected by it.

weak→functional: deliver() fixes live-confirmed (18 real deliveries incl. post-deploy), silent branches now write honest ledger rows, Trust Console panel live and correctly flagging a genuine 7-day failure. Ceiling: api-container delivery transport is structurally dead and the flagged failure has no remediation path.
Not directly re-audited; knowledge-graph lens shows decay lacks any reinforcement input (21/4,017 facts ever confirmed) and 3.4% edge density fleet-wide.

First audit of the trigger→spawn loop: a revoked Codex token killed the top workhorse/reasoning/specialty tiers for hours with green badges (29 default-closed failovers, verified alternates one slot away, never tried); catalog selection is open-loop; classification runs 28x outside its own <5s p99 SLA at ~29K tokens per routing decision.

Two of four cross-butler channels have carried zero messages ever: context bus 0 rows in 3.5 months against three hardened consumers; delegation ledger 0 rows with the tool absent from every roster prompt. Insight broker hears 3 of 9 domain voices; chronicler absent from the briefing chorus.

Trust never compounds: exact-args fingerprints make autonomy promotion mathematically unreachable (95 approvals → 53 fingerprints, max 4 < threshold 5, zero suggestions ever); rule-maturity ladder has 2 candidates and no structural consumer; graph is a star (3.4% edges).

07-10 roadmap is strong supply-side work but derived from volume skew, not manifesto promises: travel promises pre-announcement flight alerts with zero capture substrate; Gmail already captures bank e-statement PDFs the roadmap routes through a manual drop-folder; ActivityWatch is structurally single-device.

The owner's primary channel (Telegram) is a one-way, doorless, text-only pipe: voice/photo content-dropped at ingress despite deployed transcription infra, no door back to the trace spine, no deterministic command lane, and the attention ledger stamps delivery failures 'deferred' (live-confirmed) with no retry.

synthesis.qc_summary: Across four QC graders, 46 landings from the 07-10 program were graded: 34 landed-as-designed (74%), 12 landed-with-gaps, and 0 failed, regressed, or went missing — an unusually clean shipping record for ~115 commits in two days. The honesty batch is the standout (16/17 as-designed, several live-confirmed against real degraded production data — memory's pools_failed note is being exercised by an actual chronicler pool failure right now), and the QA breaker-truth batch landed 4/4 with the ledger live-verified. The worst landing by far is the deploy spine (bu-9r3hd): all five slices graded landed-with-gaps in the identical shape — mechanism real, last mile missing. The drift sentinel is blind to the stale-image failure mode that spawned it; the deployments ledger has zero frontend consumers and records an arbitrary (memory-chain) migration head; `butlers deploy` has never been used, the live redeploy having been done via the artisanal ceremony it was built to retire; the infra_state QA source was never added to the roster's enabled_sources; and the weekly restore drill is a sleep-first 7-day in-process loop that structurally cannot fire on this restart cadence. Second worst: the decisions lane (bu-ckkpz) — convention, linter, endpoint, page, and cron all real, all inert (zero labeled beads, vacuous linter, no beads mount in the dashboard-api container). bu-10fgt.4's faketime leg detected ≥3 real +45d time-bombs on its first run, then hung to GitHub's 6h kill on both legs, destroying its own evidence nightly. The meta-finding overshadowing all grades: the live stack is pinned to a frozen 07-11 04:22Z tmp-branch worktree, so a large fraction of what was graded 'landed' is not actually serving the owner, and no shipped surface says so.

themes.title: The live instrument went dark mid-program — and the deploy spine built to catch it can't see it
themes.body: Both live-stack containers bind-mount a disposable integration worktree whose HEAD is not an ancestor of main, frozen at 2026-07-11 04:22Z. Everything merged since — the tri-state breaker UI, the entire /decisions lane, honest-fan-out slices — is dark to the owner, and the drift sentinel reports is_drifted=false throughout because it compares the running image's own migration chains, not main. Every deploy-spine guarantee stops one step short on this topology: ledger unread, drill unfireable, verb unused, discovery source unenabled. The fleet's velocity is currently invisible, and grading 'landed' vs 'serving' has diverged.
themes.exemplars: docker inspect: mounts /home/tze/gt/butlers/.worktrees/compose-latest-integration-20260711 (HEAD 213664055); live GET /api/decisions → 404 (merged PR #3142); deriveBreakerState absent from serving worktree; restore_drill {checked_at:null, result:'pending'}; /api/qa/summary active_sources lacks infra_state

themes.title: Mechanism real, last mile missing — the run's signature landing gap
themes.body: All 12 landed-with-gaps grades share one shape: the mechanism ships complete and tested, but the activation step — a roster line, a compose mount, a frontend consumer, a schedule anchor, a label backfill — goes unowned, so the mechanism runs against nothing or reports to no one. This is the successor pathology to last cycle's 'backend-only honesty flags': the fleet has learned to build the whole organ but not to plug it in.
themes.exemplars: GET /api/system/deployments: zero frontend consumers; lint_decision_beads: bd list --label decision → [] (lints the empty set); dashboard-api has no .beads/issues.export.jsonl mount; restore drill sleep-first 7-day loop in a daily-restarting process; faketime leg concludes 'cancelled' not 'failure', suppressing its own alert channel; infra_state source implemented, never enabled
themes.affected: bu-9r3hd (all 5), bu-ckkpz (3 of 4), bu-10fgt.4, eco:collaboration (context bus consumers with no producers)

themes.title: Honesty reached the perimeter, not the organs — and the first false alarms now flow through honest pipes
themes.body: The degraded-flag program verifiably landed and is live-firing, but each surface's core organ still fabricates: the dashboard cost band renders a bold $0.00 on source death, the sessions table shows a partial fleet as complete history under a verdict that names the degraded pool, memory's detail trio asserts 'not in the ledger' on fetch error, education children map error to calm, QA detail routes render outages as 'not found'. Meanwhile fabrication's other direction shipped at fleet scale: /spend permanently names healthy butlers 'unavailable' (classify-before-flagging violated upstream of faithful renderers), the egress catalog presents 1.2M internal actions as an external actor, and an owner Pause renders as a fleet emergency. Both fabricated calm and fabricated alarm erode the same earned trust.
themes.exemplars: CostWidget: no error prop on the headline dollar figure; meta.unavailable_butlers=['messenger','qa','switchboard'] while /api/butlers shows all ok; FactDetailPage drops isError → 'not in the ledger'; egress actors[0]='Other / Unrecognized' 1,197,271 calls; Pause → quarantined with reason NULL

themes.title: Cross-container topology silently severs owner loops
themes.body: Multiple owner-facing loops assume everything runs in one process and break at the container boundary: deliver() resolves butler endpoints to loopback URLs valid only inside butlers-up, so every api-container notification push fails (164 attempts / 0 delivered over 7 days for a broken credential); the decisions endpoint reads a beads export no api container mounts; dashboard chat ingress is unresolvable as owner identity so the disengagement ratchet is blind to the owner's richest channel; and the attention ledger stamps these transport failures 'deferred' — a benign hold that never retries — so the trust surface itself can't distinguish chosen silence from a dead pipe.
themes.exemplars: attention ledger: secrets_lifecycle_check delivered:0 suppressed:143 deferred:21, reason 'delivery_error:...localhost:41104/mcp'; docker-compose: beads mount only on butlers-up services; identity.py has no 'dashboard' channel key; Outcome literal has no 'failed'
themes.affected: proactivity spine, decisions desk, trust console, notifications, eco:interfaces

themes.title: Stale data wearing current-data authority
themes.body: A cluster of surfaces present old state with full confidence and no age signal: the calendar grid renders a 96-day-old snapshot (provider sync silently dead since Apr 7, no error, no escalation, no plaque); model verification is 23 days stale yet silently governs routing exclusion behind ageless green badges; health KPIs show week-old vitals as current above a structurally dead freshness endpoint; education narrates a 21-day-dead curriculum build as 'the butler is still building it'; the chronicle claims 122 years of navigable history off one 1904 calendar row; /system answers 'what code is running' with a frozen v0.1.0. The common fix is the same everywhere: every asserted fact carries its age, and every feeder has a deadman.
themes.exemplars: all 10 calendar source_freshness rows stale since 2026-03-30..04-07; model_catalog last_verified_at=2026-06-19 across 31 entries; /measurements/sources → [] against 206 facts; earliest_date 1904-10-18 with a fabricated 17-hour day; MindMapGraph 'still building it' at 21 days
themes.affected: calendar, settings-models, health, education, chronicles, system

themes.title: Trust plumbing exists; trust traffic is zero
themes.body: The ecosystem lenses converge on one diagnosis: every organ of a self-trusting system has been built — context bus with vocabulary and permissions, delegation tools with a ledger, autonomy fingerprints, a rule-maturity ladder, reference counters on every fact — and none of it carries traffic. The bus has zero rows ever against three hardened consumers; delegate_ask has never been invoked and appears in no roster prompt; 95 real approvals produced zero promotion suggestions because exact-args hashing can never accumulate; recall usage is recorded on every hit and ignored by the decay formula. The vision's core success criterion — progressively earned autonomy — currently has no working mechanism, only disconnected parts.
themes.exemplars: public.user_context 0 rows / set_context 0 call sites; public.delegation_ledger 0 rows; max fingerprint count 4 < threshold 5; rules: 2 candidates, 0 consumers, rule_applications already dropped as write-orphaned; 21/4,017 facts ever confirmed

ranked_moves.what: Change isShortcutTargetSuspended's predicate from any '[role=dialog]' to '[role=dialog][aria-modal=true]', plus a target-containment check so keys typed inside any dialog never leak to the page; regression tests with a non-modal dialog mounted.

A one-line predicate change un-kills the shell's entire keyboard spine and restores the widget's own chat-while-triaging purpose.

And a down pool renders as seamless complete history in the table directly beneath a verdict opener that correctly names the degraded pool: two truths in one viewport.
